<a id="core-core-xml-writer-startdocument"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->startDocument`

```nvs skip
$writer->startDocument(): void
```

Starts the document and writes the XML declaration `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`. Call it first, before any other method. A writer writes one document, so you call this once.

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. After this call, you can write the root element.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The document is already started. The document is already finished with `endDocument`.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-enddocument"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->endDocument`

```nvs skip
$writer->endDocument(): string
```

Finishes the document and returns it as a string. Every element must be closed first. So the string this method returns is always a document that an XML parser can read.

**Returns** `string` — The whole document as a `string`. The string is not `tainted`, because the writer escaped every text and checked every name. After this call, every other method of the writer throws an error.

**Throws** `LogicError` — An element is still open. No root element was written. The document was not started with `startDocument`. The document is already finished.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-startelement"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->startElement`

```nvs skip
$writer->startElement(string $name): void
```

Opens an element, such as `<order>`. Everything you write until the matching `endElement` goes inside it. Call `attribute` right after this method to add attributes to the element.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (launder) | The element's name, such as `order` or `atom:link`. It must be a valid XML name. The writer does not escape it. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. The element is open, and the next calls write inside it.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The name is not a valid XML name. The root element is already written and closed. 1024 elements are already open inside each other. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-endelement"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->endElement`

```nvs skip
$writer->endElement(): void
```

Closes the element that `startElement` opened last. You do not pass a name, because the writer remembers which elements are open. So the end tags always match the start tags.

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. An empty element is written as `<a/>`. An element with something inside is closed with `</a>`.

**Throws** `LogicError` — No element is open. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-content"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->content`

```nvs skip
$writer->content(string $text): void
```

Writes text inside the open element. The writer escapes it: `&` becomes `&amp;`, `<` becomes `&lt;` and `>` becomes `&gt;`. A parser reads back exactly the text you wrote, so the text can never add an element or an attribute.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$text` | `string` (launder) | The text to write. It can contain any character XML allows, including `<`, `&` and quotes. A `tainted` text is allowed, because the writer escapes it. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. After this call, the writer does not indent inside this element, because added whitespace would change the text.

**Throws** `LogicError` — No element is open. The text contains a control character that XML cannot write. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-attribute"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->attribute`

```nvs skip
$writer->attribute(string $name, string $value): void
```

Adds one attribute to the element that `startElement` opened last. Call it right after `startElement`, before you write anything inside the element. The writer escapes the value, so a value can contain quotes, `<`, `&` and line breaks.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (launder) | The attribute's name, such as `id` or `xml:lang`. It must be a valid XML name. |
| `$value` | `string` (launder) | The attribute's value. When a parser reads the document, it gets back exactly this text. A `tainted` value is allowed, because the writer escapes it. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. The attribute is written in the element's start tag.

**Throws** `LogicError` — Something was already written inside the element, or no element is open. The element already has an attribute with this name. The name is not a valid XML name. The value contains a control character that XML cannot write. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-comment"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->comment`

```nvs skip
$writer->comment(string $text): void
```

Writes an XML comment, such as `<!-- note -->`. You can write it before the root element, inside an element, or after the root element is closed.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$text` | `string` (launder) | The comment's text. It is written unchanged, because XML cannot escape anything inside a comment. It cannot contain `--`, and it cannot end with `-`. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. The comment is written at the place the writer has reached.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The text contains `--` or ends with `-`. The text contains a control character that XML cannot write. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-cdata"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->cdata`

```nvs skip
$writer->cdata(string $text): void
```

Writes text inside the open element as a CDATA section, such as `<![CDATA[a < b]]>`. The text is written unchanged. A parser reads it as the same text that `content` writes.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$text` | `string` (launder) | The text to write. `<` and `&` are allowed and are not escaped. The text cannot contain `]]>`, because that ends a CDATA section. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. After this call, the writer does not indent inside this element, like after `content`.

**Throws** `LogicError` — No element is open. The text contains `]]>`. The text contains a control character that XML cannot write. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-instruction"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->instruction`

```nvs skip
$writer->instruction(string $target, string $data): void
```

Writes a processing instruction, such as `<?xml-stylesheet href="a.css"?>`. It is a note for the program that reads the document. It has a target and data, and nothing goes inside it.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$target` | `string` (sink) | The name of the program or purpose the instruction is for. It must be an XML name. It cannot be `xml` in any casing, because `startDocument` already writes that one. A `tainted` string does not compile here. |
| `$data` | `string` (sink) | The instruction's data. It is written unchanged, because XML cannot escape anything inside an instruction. It cannot contain `?>`. When it is `""`, only the target is written. A `tainted` string does not compile here, because the program that reads the document follows the data. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. The instruction is written at the place the writer has reached.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The target is not an XML name, or it is `xml`. The data contains `?>`. The data contains a control character that XML cannot write. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-xml-writer-doctype"></a>
#### `Core\Xml\Writer->doctype`

```nvs skip
$writer->doctype(string $name): void
```

Writes a document type declaration, such as `<!DOCTYPE html>`, before the root element. It writes only the name. It does not write a link to a DTD file or any entity definitions. The declaration is for programs outside Novis. `Core\Xml::parse` and `Core\Xml::reader` throw an error for any document that contains `<!DOCTYPE`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (launder) | The name of the document type. It must be an XML name. Usually it is the name of the root element. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. The declaration is written before the root element.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The root element is already started. A declaration is already written. The name is not an XML name. The document is not open.

<a id="core-core-compress"></a>
### `Core\Compress`

Keywords: compress, decompress, compressor, decompressor

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Compress::compress`](#core-core-compress-compress) | `compress(bytes\|string $data, Core\Compress::Codec $codec): bytes` |
| [`Core\Compress::decompress`](#core-core-compress-decompress) | `decompress(bytes $data, Core\Compress::Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): bytes` |
| [`Core\Compress::compressor`](#core-core-compress-compressor) | `compressor(Core\Compress::Codec $codec): Core\Compress\Compressor` |
| [`Core\Compress::decompressor`](#core-core-compress-decompressor) | `decompressor(Core\Compress::Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): Core\Compress\Decompressor` |

<a id="core-core-compress-compress"></a>
#### `Core\Compress::compress`

```nvs skip
Core\Compress::compress(bytes|string $data, Core\Compress::Codec $codec): bytes
```

Compresses `$data` in the format `$codec`. The format is a case of `Core\Compress::Codec`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$data` | `bytes\|string` | The bytes to compress. A `string` is read as its UTF-8 bytes. |
| `$codec` | `Core\Compress::Codec` | The format to write. Use `Core\Compress::Codec::Gzip` when you send the result over a network. |

**Returns** `bytes` — The compressed data, as `bytes`. Compressing has no size limit, because the output is never much larger than the input.

<a id="core-core-compress-decompress"></a>
#### `Core\Compress::decompress`

```nvs skip
Core\Compress::decompress(bytes $data, Core\Compress::Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): bytes
```

Decompresses `$data` from the format `$codec`. **The output has a size limit that cannot be switched off.**

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$data` | `bytes` | The compressed data. If `$data` is `tainted`, the result is `tainted` too. Decompressing does not make data safe to use. |
| `$codec` | `Core\Compress::Codec` | The format `$data` is in. The method does not detect the format. Data in another format throws an error. |
| `$maxBytes` | `uint` (default `67108864`) | The most output this call produces, in bytes. It can be lower than `[limits] max_decompressed`, but not higher. `0` means zero bytes. It does not mean no limit. |
| `$maxRatio` | `uint` (default `1000`) | The most bytes of output for each byte of input. This is the second part of the size limit. A compression bomb is small data that decompresses to a huge size. With a limit in bytes alone, a small request can still reach that limit. |

**Returns** `bytes` — The decompressed bytes. The result is never cut short. If the output would go over either limit, the method throws an error and returns no partial result.

**Throws** `ParseError` — `$data` is not valid data in the format `$codec`, or the output would go over either limit. It is never an `IOError`. A hostile archive and a full disk are different problems.

<a id="core-core-compress-compressor"></a>
#### `Core\Compress::compressor`

```nvs skip
Core\Compress::compressor(Core\Compress::Codec $codec): Core\Compress\Compressor
```

Starts a compression in the format `$codec` that you feed in parts. It returns a `Core\Compress\Compressor`. Call `add` to add data and `finish` to get the result.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$codec` | `Core\Compress::Codec` | The format to write, any `Core\Compress::Codec` case. It cannot change while the stream is open, because one compressed result has one format. |

**Returns** `Core\Compress\Compressor` — A new, open stream with no data in it yet.

<a id="core-core-compress-decompressor"></a>
#### `Core\Compress::decompressor`

```nvs skip
Core\Compress::decompressor(Core\Compress::Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): Core\Compress\Decompressor
```

Starts a decompression from the format `$codec` that you feed in parts. It returns a `Core\Compress\Decompressor`. Call `add` to add data and `finish` to get the result. **It has the same size limit as `decompress`, which cannot be switched off.**

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$codec` | `Core\Compress::Codec` | The format the parts are in. The method does not detect the format. Data in another format throws an error. |
| `$maxBytes` | `uint` (default `67108864`) | The most output the whole stream produces, in bytes. It is checked against `[limits] max_decompressed` when the stream starts. The limit counts all parts together. It is not a limit for each `add`. |
| `$maxRatio` | `uint` (default `1000`) | The most bytes of output for each byte added to the stream. This is the second part of the size limit. It is measured against all the data that `add` received. |

**Returns** `Core\Compress\Decompressor` — A new, open stream with no data in it yet. It has the size limit it is checked against.

<a id="core-core-compress-compressor"></a>
### `Core\Compress\Compressor`

Keywords: add, finish

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Compress\Compressor->add`](#core-core-compress-compressor-add) | `add(bytes\|string $data): void` |
| [`Core\Compress\Compressor->finish`](#core-core-compress-compressor-finish) | `finish(): bytes` |

<a id="core-core-compress-compressor-add"></a>
#### `Core\Compress\Compressor->add`

```nvs skip
$compressor->add(bytes|string $data): void
```

Adds `$data` to the stream. `finish` compresses all parts in the order they were added.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$data` | `bytes\|string` | The next bytes. A `string` is read as its UTF-8 bytes. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. `finish` returns all the compressed data at once.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The stream is already finished. Its result is complete, so start a new stream.

<a id="core-core-compress-compressor-finish"></a>
#### `Core\Compress\Compressor->finish`

```nvs skip
$compressor->finish(): bytes
```

Closes the stream and returns all the data that `add` received, compressed. The result is the same bytes `Core\Compress::compress` returns for all the parts joined.

**Returns** `bytes` — The compressed data, as `bytes`. After the call, the stream is finished and its parts are freed. The result is not `tainted`, even when the input is. Compressed data is not read as text anywhere.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The stream is already finished. A second `finish` throws this error and returns nothing.

<a id="core-core-compress-decompressor"></a>
### `Core\Compress\Decompressor`

Keywords: add, finish

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Compress\Decompressor->add`](#core-core-compress-decompressor-add) | `add(bytes $data): void` |
| [`Core\Compress\Decompressor->finish`](#core-core-compress-decompressor-finish) | `finish(): tainted bytes` |

<a id="core-core-compress-decompressor-add"></a>
#### `Core\Compress\Decompressor->add`

```nvs skip
$decompressor->add(bytes $data): void
```

Adds `$data` to the stream. `finish` decompresses all parts in the order they were added, with the size limit the stream started with.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$data` | `bytes` | The next bytes of the compressed data. Nothing is decompressed yet, so this call never throws a size error. `finish` checks the size limit for the whole stream. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. The size limit counts the whole stream, not each call.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The stream is already finished. Its data cannot change, so start a new stream.

<a id="core-core-compress-decompressor-finish"></a>
#### `Core\Compress\Decompressor->finish`

```nvs skip
$decompressor->finish(): tainted bytes
```

Closes the stream and returns all the data that `add` received, decompressed. The result is the same bytes `Core\Compress::decompress` returns for all the parts joined, with the same size limit.

**Returns** `tainted bytes` — The decompressed data as `tainted bytes`. The result is never cut short. After the call, the stream is finished and its parts are freed. The bytes are `tainted` because they come from input the program does not control.

**Throws** `ParseError` — The parts are not valid data in the stream's format, or the output would go over either limit the stream started with. The limit counts all parts together.; `RuntimeError` — The stream is already finished. This is also true after a `finish` that threw an error.

<a id="core-core-mime"></a>
### `Core\Mime`

Keywords: detect, mediaType

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Mime::detect`](#core-core-mime-detect) | `detect(bytes $data): Core\Mime::Type` |
| [`Core\Mime::mediaType`](#core-core-mime-mediatype) | `mediaType(Core\Mime::Type $type): string` |

<a id="core-core-mime-detect"></a>
#### `Core\Mime::detect`

```nvs skip
Core\Mime::detect(bytes $data): Core\Mime::Type
```

Returns the type of `$data`, read from the bytes themselves. There is no parameter for a file name, because an attacker can choose a file name's extension.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$data` | `bytes` (neutral) | The bytes to check. Only the first 16 bytes or fewer are read. So the start of an upload gives the same result as the whole upload. |

**Returns** `Core\Mime::Type` — The case for the kind of file. It is `Core\Mime::Type::Unknown` when no format matches, and for every text format. **The result does not make the data safe.** Bytes detected as `image/png` are still `tainted`, because only the first bytes were checked.

<a id="core-core-mime-mediatype"></a>
#### `Core\Mime::mediaType`

```nvs skip
Core\Mime::mediaType(Core\Mime::Type $type): string
```

Returns the IANA media type of `$type`, for a `Content-Type` header or a stored record. There is no method that turns a media type back into a case.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$type` | `Core\Mime::Type` | The case to convert, usually one that `detect` returned. |

**Returns** `string` — The media type as a string, such as `image/png`. For `Core\Mime::Type::Unknown` it is `application/octet-stream`, the usual type for bytes of an unknown kind.

<a id="core-core-zip"></a>
### `Core\Zip`

Keywords: entries, read, extract

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Zip::entries`](#core-core-zip-entries) | `entries(bytes $archive): array<tainted string>` |
| [`Core\Zip::read`](#core-core-zip-read) | `read(bytes $archive, string $name, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): tainted bytes` |
| [`Core\Zip::extract`](#core-core-zip-extract) | `extract(bytes $archive, string $destination, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): uint` |

<a id="core-core-zip-entries"></a>
#### `Core\Zip::entries`

```nvs skip
Core\Zip::entries(bytes $archive): array<tainted string>
```

Returns the names of the entries in an archive, in the order its central directory lists them. The whole archive is checked first. If one entry uses `..`, an absolute path or a symlink, it throws an error and lists nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$archive` | `bytes` (neutral) | The bytes of the archive. Only its central directory is read. So the time to list an archive depends on the number of entries, not on the size of the archive. |

**Returns** `array<tainted string>` — One `tainted string` per entry. A name is always tainted, whatever the type of the archive was. The name was written by whoever built the archive. An archive written directly in a test is no safer than a downloaded one.

**Throws** `ParseError` — `$archive` is not a valid zip archive, or one of its entries is unsafe. An entry is unsafe when it has an absolute path or a `..` part, or is a symlink. It is also unsafe when it is nested in more than 64 folders, or repeats a name. A bad archive never throws an `IOError`. That error is for a failing disk.

<a id="core-core-zip-read"></a>
#### `Core\Zip::read`

```nvs skip
Core\Zip::read(bytes $archive, string $name, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): tainted bytes
```

Returns the decompressed bytes of one entry. **The output has a size limit that cannot be switched off.**

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$archive` | `bytes` (neutral) | The bytes of the archive. It is checked the same way as in `entries`. An unsafe entry anywhere in the archive makes this call throw too, whichever entry you read. |
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The entry to read. It is compared with the names in the archive exactly, and it is never treated as a path. A name that `entries` returned works as it is. |
| `$maxBytes` | `uint` (default `67108864`) | The largest output this call may produce, in bytes. It can be lower than `[limits] max_decompressed`, but not higher. `0` means zero bytes, not unlimited. |
| `$maxRatio` | `uint` (default `1000`) | The largest output per byte of the compressed entry. This is the second part of the size limit, because a zip bomb is small before it is decompressed. |

**Returns** `tainted bytes` — All the bytes of the entry. The result is never cut short. An entry larger than either limit throws an error. The bytes are `tainted`, like the names, because somebody else wrote the archive.

**Throws** `ParseError` — Every case where `entries` throws. It is also thrown when no entry has that name, or the entry uses a compression method this class cannot read. Other causes are a broken compressed stream, a wrong CRC-32, or output above either limit.

<a id="core-core-zip-extract"></a>
#### `Core\Zip::extract`

```nvs skip
Core\Zip::extract(bytes $archive, string $destination, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): uint
```

Writes the entries of an archive under `$destination` and returns how many files it wrote. The whole archive is checked before any byte is written. Each directory is created and then checked to be inside `$destination`, before anything is written into it.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$archive` | `bytes` (neutral) | The bytes of the archive. It is checked the same way as in `entries`. An unsafe entry anywhere in the archive makes this call throw before it writes anything. |
| `$destination` | `string` (sink) | The directory to write the files to. It is created if it does not exist. The call needs `fs.write` and also `fs.read` for it, because Novis reads the directories above a name to find where it points. |
| `$maxBytes` | `uint` (default `67108864`) | The largest output this call may produce **for the whole archive**, in bytes. It is not a limit per entry. Many small entries can add up to an attack too. It can be lower than `[limits] max_decompressed`, but not higher. |
| `$maxRatio` | `uint` (default `1000`) | The largest output per byte of a compressed entry. This limit is per entry, because each entry is decompressed on its own. |

**Returns** `uint` — The number of files written. A directory entry is created, but it is not counted. So the number is the number of new files.

**Throws** `ParseError` — Every case where `entries` throws. It is also thrown for a wrong CRC-32, or for output above either limit, per entry or for the whole archive.; `RuntimeError` — `fs.read` or `fs.write` is not granted for the destination. It is also thrown when a directory inside it points outside it. This happens when somebody creates a link while the files are written.; `IOError` — Creating or writing a file failed. A file with the name of an entry may already exist, because `extract` never overwrites a file. Or the disk failed. The safety checks of this class throw a `ParseError` or a `RuntimeError` instead.

<a id="core-core-http"></a>
### `Core\Http`

Keywords: allowUrl, methodName

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|

<a id="core-core-http-allowurl"></a>
#### `Core\Http::allowUrl`

```nvs skip
Core\Http::allowUrl(string $url): Core\Http\Target
```

Checks `$url` against the outbound policy. It checks the scheme, the `net.connect` grant and the addresses the host resolves to. The result contains the approved addresses.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$url` | `string` (launder) | The URL to check. A `tainted` URL is allowed here. No other outbound call accepts one. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Target` — A `Core\Http\Target` with every address of the host that the policy approved. It has at most eight addresses, in the order the name lookup returned them. The client connects only to these addresses, so a second name lookup cannot change them.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The text is not a URL, its scheme is not `http` or `https`, or it has no host. Or `net.connect` does not grant the host, or the host resolves to no address. Or the host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unspecified address that `net.internal` does not list.

<a id="core-core-http-methodname"></a>
#### `Core\Http::methodName`

```nvs skip
Core\Http::methodName(Core\Http\Method $method): string
```

Returns the name of an HTTP method as it is written in a request and in an `Allow` header. `Core\Http\Method::Get` gives `GET`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$method` | `Core\Http\Method` | The method, as a case of `Core\Http\Method`. |

**Returns** `string` — The name in capital letters: `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `TRACE`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`.

<a id="core-core-http-identity"></a>
### `Core\Http\Identity`

Keywords: read

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Http\Identity::read`](#core-core-http-identity-read) | `read(bytes $chainPem, Core\Crypto\KeyPair $key): Core\Http\Identity` |

<a id="core-core-http-identity-read"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Identity::read`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Identity::read(bytes $chainPem, Core\Crypto\KeyPair $key): Core\Http\Identity
```

Reads a client certificate chain and its private key. A request sends them when a server asks the client for a certificate. The leaf certificate is checked against the key here. If they do not match, this throws an error before any connection is opened.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$chainPem` | `bytes` (neutral) | The chain as PEM. The leaf certificate comes first, then the intermediate certificates the server needs to check it. Other HTTP clients use the same order. |
| `$key` | `Core\Crypto\KeyPair` | The private key of the leaf certificate. The TLS handshake is signed with this key. A key that can only do key agreement, such as `X25519`, throws an error. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Identity` — The identity. Pass it as a request's `identity` option. It is sent only when the server asks for it. Two different identities never share a pooled connection.

**Throws** `LogicError` — `$chainPem` is not a PEM certificate chain, or it contains no certificate. Or `$key` cannot sign a TLS handshake. Or the leaf certificate has a different public key from `$key`. A client identity is part of the program's own deployment, so this error always means a mistake in the deployed files.

<a id="core-core-http-client-get"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Client::get`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Client::get(string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, followRedirects?: uint, retryAttempts?: uint, retryBackoff?: Core\Time\Duration, retryIdempotencyKey?: string, json?: mixed, form?: array<secret tainted string>, body?: secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes|Core\Http\Part, contentType?: string, multipart?: array<secret tainted string|Core\Http\Part>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, redirectToHttp?: bool }): Core\Http\Response
```

Sends a `GET` request to `$url`, with a time limit. It connects only to an address that the outbound policy approved.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$url` | `string\|Core\Http\Target` (sink) | Where the request goes. It is a URL that the program wrote, or a `Core\Http\Target` from `Core\Http::allowUrl`. A `tainted` URL is not allowed here. Check it with `Core\Http::allowUrl` first. |
| `{ deadline: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The time limit for the whole call. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] deadline` is used. There is no way to write a call with no deadline. |
| `{ connectTimeout: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | How long the connection alone may take. This time is part of `deadline`, and is not added to it. |
| `{ headers: … }` | `array<secret string>` (default `[]`) | Extra request headers, by name. A `secret` value is allowed here, because a credential must reach the API it is for. A `tainted` value is not allowed. The runtime adds its own headers as well. |
| `{ followRedirects: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | How many redirects to follow. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] max_redirects` is used, and its default is `0`. Each redirect is checked against the outbound policy again, and its address is approved again. |
| `{ retryAttempts: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | The total number of attempts, including the first. `1` is the same as the default, and `0` throws an error. Retries wait a random delay (jitter), and all attempts share one deadline. |
| `{ retryBackoff: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The base delay between retries. The delay grows exponentially, and each wait is a random time up to that delay (full jitter). If it is not given, it is `100ms`. You cannot configure the jitter. |
| `{ retryIdempotencyKey: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | Sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header, with the same value on every attempt. It is required for `post` and `patch` when `retryAttempts` is given. Every other method also accepts it. |
| `{ json: … }` | `mixed` (default `(omitted)`) | The value to send as `application/json`. It is encoded once for the whole call. A `secret` inside it is sent, as it is in a header. A `null` value sends the JSON document `null`, not an empty body. |
| `{ form: … }` | `array<secret tainted string>` (default `null`) | The fields to send as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, by name. |
| `{ body: … }` | `secret tainted string\|secret tainted bytes\|Core\Http\Part` (default `null`) | The bytes to send exactly as given, with the media type in `contentType`. Only one of `json`, `form`, `body` and `multipart` may be given. None of them is allowed on `get` or `head`. Both mistakes are compile errors. |
| `{ contentType: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The media type of `body`. It has no effect without `body`, so giving it alone is a compile error. |
| `{ multipart: … }` | `array<secret tainted string\|Core\Http\Part>` (default `null`) | The parts to send as `multipart/form-data`, by name. |
| `{ identity: … }` | `Core\Http\Identity` (default `null`) | The client certificate to send when the server asks for one. Create it with `Core\Http\Identity::read`. Nothing is sent to a server that does not ask. Two different identities never share a pooled connection. A call without an identity does not share one with a call that has one. |
| `{ tlsCa: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the `anchors` grant of `capabilities.tls`. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects. |
| `{ tlsPin: … }` | `string\|array<string>` (default `null`, neutral) | One `sha256//<base64>` public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the `pin` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerifyHost: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the `any_name` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerify: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the `insecure` grant. |
| `{ tlsMinVersion: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The lowest TLS version this call allows, `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's `[http.client.tls] min_version` throws an error. |
| `{ connectTo: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the `net.connect_to` grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a `Core\Http\Target` as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses. |
| `{ redirectToHttp: … }` | `bool` (default `false`) | If it is `true`, a redirect from `https` to plain `http` may be followed. The redirect's host must also be in the `net.downgrade` grant. If it is not given, such a redirect throws an error. Otherwise one `Location` header would be enough for a server to remove a call's TLS. This option does not affect a plain `http` URL that you request directly. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Response` — A `Core\Http\Response` with the status and the body of the reply. A `404` or a `500` is a normal reply and is returned here. Only a request that gets no reply at all throws an error. An `https` URL is fetched over TLS. The certificate is checked against the certificate authorities that Novis includes.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not `http` or `https`, or it has no host. Or `net.connect` does not grant the host. Or the host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unspecified address that `net.internal` does not list. An option is out of range. A `deadline`, `connectTimeout` or `retryBackoff` is not a positive duration. On `stream`, the same is true for `idle` and `maxDuration`. Or `retryAttempts` is zero. A header name or value contains a control byte, which would end the line early. An `https` server sent a certificate that does not verify against the certificate authorities Novis includes. Or the certificate is not valid for that name. Or the reply is not HTTP, or it is larger than the limit for one request. A body that is not text does not cause this error. `Core\Http\Response::text` throws for it. `request` gets the method as a value, so it checks two things before the first attempt. The other methods check them at compile time. The first is a body option on a `Get` or a `Head`. The second is retries on a `Post` or a `Patch` without `retryIdempotencyKey`.; `TimeoutError` — The `deadline` passed before a reply arrived. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If a wait would end after the deadline, the error is thrown at once, without waiting.; `IOError` — The last attempt could not reach the pinned address, or the connection failed while the request was being sent or the reply read.

<a id="core-core-http-client-post"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Client::post`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Client::post(string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, followRedirects?: uint, retryAttempts?: uint, retryBackoff?: Core\Time\Duration, retryIdempotencyKey?: string, json?: mixed, form?: array<secret tainted string>, body?: secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes|Core\Http\Part, contentType?: string, multipart?: array<secret tainted string|Core\Http\Part>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, redirectToHttp?: bool }): Core\Http\Response

A header name or value contains a control byte, which would end the line early. An `https` server sent a certificate that does not verify against the certificate authorities Novis includes. Or the certificate is not valid for that name. Or the reply is not HTTP, or it is larger than the limit for one request. A body that is not text does not cause this error. `Core\Http\Response::text` throws for it. `request` gets the method as a value, so it checks two things before the first attempt. The other methods check them at compile time. The first is a body option on a `Get` or a `Head`. The second is retries on a `Post` or a `Patch` without `retryIdempotencyKey`.; `TimeoutError` — The `deadline` passed before a reply arrived. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If a wait would end after the deadline, the error is thrown at once, without waiting.; `IOError` — The last attempt could not reach the pinned address, or the connection failed while the request was being sent or the reply read.

<a id="core-core-http-client-patch"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Client::patch`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Client::patch(string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, followRedirects?: uint, retryAttempts?: uint, retryBackoff?: Core\Time\Duration, retryIdempotencyKey?: string, json?: mixed, form?: array<secret tainted string>, body?: secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes|Core\Http\Part, contentType?: string, multipart?: array<secret tainted string|Core\Http\Part>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, redirectToHttp?: bool }): Core\Http\Response
```

Sends a `PATCH` request to `$url`, with a time limit. A repeated partial update can make the change twice, so retries need `retryIdempotencyKey`, as for `post`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$url` | `string\|Core\Http\Target` (sink) | Where the request goes. It is a URL that the program wrote, or a `Core\Http\Target` from `Core\Http::allowUrl`. A `tainted` URL is not allowed here. Check it with `Core\Http::allowUrl` first. |
| `{ deadline: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The time limit for the whole call. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] deadline` is used. There is no way to write a call with no deadline. |
| `{ connectTimeout: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | How long the connection alone may take. This time is part of `deadline`, and is not added to it. |
| `{ headers: … }` | `array<secret string>` (default `[]`) | Extra request headers, by name. A `secret` value is allowed here, because a credential must reach the API it is for. A `tainted` value is not allowed. The runtime adds its own headers as well. |
| `{ followRedirects: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | How many redirects to follow. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] max_redirects` is used, and its default is `0`. Each redirect is checked against the outbound policy again, and its address is approved again. |
| `{ retryAttempts: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | The total number of attempts, including the first. `1` is the same as the default, and `0` throws an error. Retries wait a random delay (jitter), and all attempts share one deadline. |
| `{ retryBackoff: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The base delay between retries. The delay grows exponentially, and each wait is a random time up to that delay (full jitter). If it is not given, it is `100ms`. You cannot configure the jitter. |
| `{ retryIdempotencyKey: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | Sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header, with the same value on every attempt. It is required for `post` and `patch` when `retryAttempts` is given. Every other method also accepts it. |
| `{ json: … }` | `mixed` (default `(omitted)`) | The value to send as `application/json`. It is encoded once for the whole call. A `secret` inside it is sent, as it is in a header. A `null` value sends the JSON document `null`, not an empty body. |
| `{ form: … }` | `array<secret tainted string>` (default `null`) | The fields to send as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, by name. |
| `{ body: … }` | `secret tainted string\|secret tainted bytes\|Core\Http\Part` (default `null`) | The bytes to send exactly as given, with the media type in `contentType`. Only one of `json`, `form`, `body` and `multipart` may be given. None of them is allowed on `get` or `head`. Both mistakes are compile errors. |
| `{ contentType: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The media type of `body`. It has no effect without `body`, so giving it alone is a compile error. |
| `{ multipart: … }` | `array<secret tainted string\|Core\Http\Part>` (default `null`) | The parts to send as `multipart/form-data`, by name. |
| `{ identity: … }` | `Core\Http\Identity` (default `null`) | The client certificate to send when the server asks for one. Create it with `Core\Http\Identity::read`. Nothing is sent to a server that does not ask. Two different identities never share a pooled connection. A call without an identity does not share one with a call that has one. |
| `{ tlsCa: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the `anchors` grant of `capabilities.tls`. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects. |
| `{ tlsPin: … }` | `string\|array<string>` (default `null`, neutral) | One `sha256//<base64>` public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the `pin` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerifyHost: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the `any_name` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerify: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the `insecure` grant. |
| `{ tlsMinVersion: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The lowest TLS version this call allows, `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's `[http.client.tls] min_version` throws an error. |
| `{ connectTo: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the `net.connect_to` grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a `Core\Http\Target` as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses. |
| `{ redirectToHttp: … }` | `bool` (default `false`) | If it is `true`, a redirect from `https` to plain `http` may be followed. The redirect's host must also be in the `net.downgrade` grant. If it is not given, such a redirect throws an error. Otherwise one `Location` header would be enough for a server to remove a call's TLS. This option does not affect a plain `http` URL that you request directly. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Response` — A `Core\Http\Response` with the status and the body of the reply. A `404` or a `500` is a normal reply and is returned here. Only a request that gets no reply at all throws an error. An `https` URL is fetched over TLS. The certificate is checked against the certificate authorities that Novis includes.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not `http` or `https`, or it has no host. Or `net.connect` does not grant the host. Or the host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unspecified address that `net.internal` does not list. An option is out of range. A `deadline`, `connectTimeout` or `retryBackoff` is not a positive duration. On `stream`, the same is true for `idle` and `maxDuration`. Or `retryAttempts` is zero. A header name or value contains a control byte, which would end the line early. An `https` server sent a certificate that does not verify against the certificate authorities Novis includes. Or the certificate is not valid for that name. Or the reply is not HTTP, or it is larger than the limit for one request. A body that is not text does not cause this error. `Core\Http\Response::text` throws for it. `request` gets the method as a value, so it checks two things before the first attempt. The other methods check them at compile time. The first is a body option on a `Get` or a `Head`. The second is retries on a `Post` or a `Patch` without `retryIdempotencyKey`.; `TimeoutError` — The `deadline` passed before a reply arrived. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If a wait would end after the deadline, the error is thrown at once, without waiting.; `IOError` — The last attempt could not reach the pinned address, or the connection failed while the request was being sent or the reply read.

<a id="core-core-http-client-request"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Client::request`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Client::request(Core\Http\Method $method, string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, followRedirects?: uint, retryAttempts?: uint, retryBackoff?: Core\Time\Duration, retryIdempotencyKey?: string, json?: mixed, form?: array<secret tainted string>, body?: secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes|Core\Http\Part, contentType?: string, multipart?: array<secret tainted string|Core\Http\Part>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, redirectToHttp?: bool }): Core\Http\Response

| `{ headers: … }` | `array<secret string>` (default `[]`) | Extra request headers, by name. A `secret` value is allowed here, because a credential must reach the API it is for. A `tainted` value is not allowed. The runtime adds its own headers as well. |
| `{ followRedirects: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | How many redirects to follow. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] max_redirects` is used, and its default is `0`. Each redirect is checked against the outbound policy again, and its address is approved again. |
| `{ retryAttempts: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | The total number of attempts, including the first. `1` is the same as the default, and `0` throws an error. Retries wait a random delay (jitter), and all attempts share one deadline. |
| `{ retryBackoff: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The base delay between retries. The delay grows exponentially, and each wait is a random time up to that delay (full jitter). If it is not given, it is `100ms`. You cannot configure the jitter. |
| `{ retryIdempotencyKey: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | Sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header, with the same value on every attempt. It is required for `post` and `patch` when `retryAttempts` is given. Every other method also accepts it. |
| `{ json: … }` | `mixed` (default `(omitted)`) | The value to send as `application/json`. It is encoded once for the whole call. A `secret` inside it is sent, as it is in a header. A `null` value sends the JSON document `null`, not an empty body. |
| `{ form: … }` | `array<secret tainted string>` (default `null`) | The fields to send as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, by name. |
| `{ body: … }` | `secret tainted string\|secret tainted bytes\|Core\Http\Part` (default `null`) | The bytes to send exactly as given, with the media type in `contentType`. Only one of `json`, `form`, `body` and `multipart` may be given. None of them is allowed on `get` or `head`. Both mistakes are compile errors. |
| `{ contentType: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The media type of `body`. It has no effect without `body`, so giving it alone is a compile error. |
| `{ multipart: … }` | `array<secret tainted string\|Core\Http\Part>` (default `null`) | The parts to send as `multipart/form-data`, by name. |
| `{ identity: … }` | `Core\Http\Identity` (default `null`) | The client certificate to send when the server asks for one. Create it with `Core\Http\Identity::read`. Nothing is sent to a server that does not ask. Two different identities never share a pooled connection. A call without an identity does not share one with a call that has one. |
| `{ tlsCa: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the `anchors` grant of `capabilities.tls`. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects. |
| `{ tlsPin: … }` | `string\|array<string>` (default `null`, neutral) | One `sha256//<base64>` public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the `pin` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerifyHost: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the `any_name` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerify: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the `insecure` grant. |
| `{ tlsMinVersion: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The lowest TLS version this call allows, `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's `[http.client.tls] min_version` throws an error. |
| `{ connectTo: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the `net.connect_to` grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a `Core\Http\Target` as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses. |
| `{ redirectToHttp: … }` | `bool` (default `false`) | If it is `true`, a redirect from `https` to plain `http` may be followed. The redirect's host must also be in the `net.downgrade` grant. If it is not given, such a redirect throws an error. Otherwise one `Location` header would be enough for a server to remove a call's TLS. This option does not affect a plain `http` URL that you request directly. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Response` — A `Core\Http\Response` with the status and the body of the reply. A `404` or a `500` is a normal reply and is returned here. Only a request that gets no reply at all throws an error. An `https` URL is fetched over TLS. The certificate is checked against the certificate authorities that Novis includes.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not `http` or `https`, or it has no host. Or `net.connect` does not grant the host. Or the host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unspecified address that `net.internal` does not list. An option is out of range. A `deadline`, `connectTimeout` or `retryBackoff` is not a positive duration. On `stream`, the same is true for `idle` and `maxDuration`. Or `retryAttempts` is zero. A header name or value contains a control byte, which would end the line early. An `https` server sent a certificate that does not verify against the certificate authorities Novis includes. Or the certificate is not valid for that name. Or the reply is not HTTP, or it is larger than the limit for one request. A body that is not text does not cause this error. `Core\Http\Response::text` throws for it. `request` gets the method as a value, so it checks two things before the first attempt. The other methods check them at compile time. The first is a body option on a `Get` or a `Head`. The second is retries on a `Post` or a `Patch` without `retryIdempotencyKey`.; `TimeoutError` — The `deadline` passed before a reply arrived. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If a wait would end after the deadline, the error is thrown at once, without waiting.; `IOError` — The last attempt could not reach the pinned address, or the connection failed while the request was being sent or the reply read.

<a id="core-core-http-client-stream"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Client::stream`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Client::stream(Core\Http\Method $method, string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, followRedirects?: uint, retryAttempts?: uint, retryBackoff?: Core\Time\Duration, retryIdempotencyKey?: string, json?: mixed, form?: array<secret tainted string>, body?: secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes|Core\Http\Part, contentType?: string, multipart?: array<secret tainted string|Core\Http\Part>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, redirectToHttp?: bool, idle?: Core\Time\Duration, maxDuration?: Core\Time\Duration }): Core\Http\Stream
```

Sends a request with `$method` to `$url`, and returns when the status and headers arrive. The program then reads the body as it comes. Use it for a reply that is read piece by piece, such as server-sent events or a result set one line at a time.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$method` | `Core\Http\Method` | The HTTP method to send, as a `Core\Http\Method` case. A `Post` or a `Patch` with retries but without `retryIdempotencyKey` throws an error before the first attempt. The methods `post` and `patch` give a compile error for the same mistake. |
| `$url` | `string\|Core\Http\Target` (sink) | Where the request goes. It is a URL that the program wrote, or a `Core\Http\Target` from `Core\Http::allowUrl`. A `tainted` URL is not allowed here. Check it with `Core\Http::allowUrl` first. |
| `{ deadline: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The time limit for the whole call. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] deadline` is used. There is no way to write a call with no deadline. |
| `{ connectTimeout: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | How long the connection alone may take. This time is part of `deadline`, and is not added to it. |
| `{ headers: … }` | `array<secret string>` (default `[]`) | Extra request headers, by name. A `secret` value is allowed here, because a credential must reach the API it is for. A `tainted` value is not allowed. The runtime adds its own headers as well. |
| `{ followRedirects: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | How many redirects to follow. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] max_redirects` is used, and its default is `0`. Each redirect is checked against the outbound policy again, and its address is approved again. |
| `{ retryAttempts: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | The total number of attempts, including the first. `1` is the same as the default, and `0` throws an error. Retries wait a random delay (jitter), and all attempts share one deadline. |
| `{ retryBackoff: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The base delay between retries. The delay grows exponentially, and each wait is a random time up to that delay (full jitter). If it is not given, it is `100ms`. You cannot configure the jitter. |
| `{ retryIdempotencyKey: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | Sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header, with the same value on every attempt. It is required for `post` and `patch` when `retryAttempts` is given. Every other method also accepts it. |
| `{ json: … }` | `mixed` (default `(omitted)`) | The value to send as `application/json`. It is encoded once for the whole call. A `secret` inside it is sent, as it is in a header. A `null` value sends the JSON document `null`, not an empty body. |
| `{ form: … }` | `array<secret tainted string>` (default `null`) | The fields to send as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, by name. |
| `{ body: … }` | `secret tainted string\|secret tainted bytes\|Core\Http\Part` (default `null`) | The bytes to send exactly as given, with the media type in `contentType`. Only one of `json`, `form`, `body` and `multipart` may be given. None of them is allowed on `get` or `head`. Both mistakes are compile errors. |
| `{ contentType: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The media type of `body`. It has no effect without `body`, so giving it alone is a compile error. |
| `{ multipart: … }` | `array<secret tainted string\|Core\Http\Part>` (default `null`) | The parts to send as `multipart/form-data`, by name. |
| `{ identity: … }` | `Core\Http\Identity` (default `null`) | The client certificate to send when the server asks for one. Create it with `Core\Http\Identity::read`. Nothing is sent to a server that does not ask. Two different identities never share a pooled connection. A call without an identity does not share one with a call that has one. |
| `{ tlsCa: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the `anchors` grant of `capabilities.tls`. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects. |
| `{ tlsPin: … }` | `string\|array<string>` (default `null`, neutral) | One `sha256//<base64>` public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the `pin` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerifyHost: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the `any_name` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerify: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the `insecure` grant. |
| `{ tlsMinVersion: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The lowest TLS version this call allows, `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's `[http.client.tls] min_version` throws an error. |
| `{ connectTo: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the `net.connect_to` grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a `Core\Http\Target` as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses. |
| `{ redirectToHttp: … }` | `bool` (default `false`) | If it is `true`, a redirect from `https` to plain `http` may be followed. The redirect's host must also be in the `net.downgrade` grant. If it is not given, such a redirect throws an error. Otherwise one `Location` header would be enough for a server to remove a call's TLS. This option does not affect a plain `http` URL that you request directly. |
| `{ idle: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The longest time the body may be silent after the status and headers arrive. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] idle` is used. There is no way to turn this limit off. |
| `{ maxDuration: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The longest time the whole body may take. This limit stops a server that sends one byte at a time, just often enough to pass the `idle` check. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] max_duration` is used. `deadline` covers only the connection, the status and the headers. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Stream` — A `Core\Http\Stream`. Its `status()`, `header()` and `headers()` methods return the status and headers. Read the body with exactly one of `events()`, `lines()`, `chunks()` and `saveTo()`.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not `http` or `https`, or it has no host. Or `net.connect` does not grant the host. Or the host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unspecified address that `net.internal` does not list. An option is out of range. A `deadline`, `connectTimeout` or `retryBackoff` is not a positive duration. On `stream`, the same is true for `idle` and `maxDuration`. Or `retryAttempts` is zero. A header name or value contains a control byte, which would end the line early. An `https` server sent a certificate that does not verify against the certificate authorities Novis includes. Or the certificate is not valid for that name. Or the reply is not HTTP, or it is larger than the limit for one request. A body that is not text does not cause this error. `Core\Http\Response::text` throws for it. `request` gets the method as a value, so it checks two things before the first attempt. The other methods check them at compile time. The first is a body option on a `Get` or a `Head`. The second is retries on a `Post` or a `Patch` without `retryIdempotencyKey`.; `TimeoutError` — The `deadline` passed before a reply arrived. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If a wait would end after the deadline, the error is thrown at once, without waiting.; `IOError` — The last attempt could not reach the pinned address, or the connection failed while the request was being sent or the reply read.

<a id="core-core-http-client-opensocket"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Client::openSocket`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Client::openSocket(string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, protocols?: array<string>, idle?: Core\Time\Duration, maxDuration?: Core\Time\Duration, maxMessage?: uint, sendTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, ping?: Core\Time\Duration }): Core\Http\Socket
```

Opens a WebSocket to `$url`, and returns it when the server's `101` reply arrives. Use it for a realtime API that the program keeps talking to.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$url` | `string\|Core\Http\Target` (sink) | The server to open the socket to. It is a `ws` or `wss` URL that the program wrote, or a `Core\Http\Target` from `Core\Http::allowUrl`. An `http` or `https` URL is not allowed here. A `tainted` URL must be checked with `Core\Http::allowUrl` first. |
| `{ deadline: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The time limit for the opening handshake. It covers the connection and every address tried, and it ends when the `101` reply arrives. After that, `idle` and `maxDuration` limit the conversation. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] deadline` is used. There is no way to write a socket with no deadline. |
| `{ connectTimeout: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | How long the connection alone may take. This time is part of `deadline`, and is not added to it. |
| `{ headers: … }` | `array<secret string>` (default `[]`) | Extra request headers, by name. A `secret` value is allowed here, because a credential must reach the API it is for. A `tainted` value is not allowed. The runtime adds its own headers as well. |
| `{ identity: … }` | `Core\Http\Identity` (default `null`) | The client certificate to send when the server asks for one. Create it with `Core\Http\Identity::read`. Nothing is sent to a server that does not ask. Two different identities never share a pooled connection. A call without an identity does not share one with a call that has one. |
| `{ tlsCa: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the `anchors` grant of `capabilities.tls`. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects. |
| `{ tlsPin: … }` | `string\|array<string>` (default `null`, neutral) | One `sha256//<base64>` public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the `pin` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerifyHost: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the `any_name` grant. |
| `{ tlsVerify: … }` | `bool` (default `true`) | If it is `false`, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the `insecure` grant. |
| `{ tlsMinVersion: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The lowest TLS version this call allows, `"1.2"` or `"1.3"`. It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's `[http.client.tls] min_version` throws an error. |
| `{ connectTo: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the `net.connect_to` grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a `Core\Http\Target` as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses. |
| `{ protocols: … }` | `array<string>` (default `[]`) | The subprotocols to offer in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, most preferred first. Each name is one word of letters, digits and the punctuation an HTTP token allows, such as `.`, `-` and `_`. A space, a comma or a control character throws an error. `Core\Http\Socket::protocol` returns the one the server chooses. If the server chooses a name that was not offered, the call throws an error. |
| `{ idle: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The longest time the socket may be silent in either direction. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] idle` is used. There is no way to turn this limit off. With `ping` set, a live but quiet server answers the pings, so only a dead server reaches this limit. |
| `{ maxDuration: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The longest time the socket may stay open in total. This limit stops a server that sends one frame at a time, just often enough to pass the `idle` check. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client] max_duration` is used. |
| `{ maxMessage: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | The largest message, in bytes, that this side builds from the server's fragments. A larger message closes the socket with code `1009`. The waiting `receive` then throws an error that names the limit. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client.socket] max_message` is used. |
| `{ sendTimeout: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The longest time a frame may wait to be sent to a server that is not reading. It is also how long `close` waits for the server's own close frame. If it is not given, the runtime's `[http.client.socket] send_timeout` is used. |
| `{ ping: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | How long the socket stays silent before it sends a ping. A live server answers the ping, so `idle` closes only a dead connection. If it is not given, no ping is sent, because a ping is traffic the server did not ask for. A ping from the server is always answered, because the WebSocket protocol requires it. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Socket` — A `Core\Http\Socket` for the conversation. `receive()` returns the server's next message as a `Core\Socket\Message`, the same class a server-side connection uses. `send()` and `sendBytes()` send the two kinds of message, and `close()` ends the conversation. The socket belongs to the task that opened it. It is closed with code `1001` when that task ends, so it never lives longer than its request, command or job.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not `ws` or `wss`, or it has no host. This method does not accept `http` or `https`, and the other methods do not accept `ws` or `wss`. Or `net.connect` does not grant the host, or the host resolves to an address the deployment's policy denies. An option is out of range. A `deadline`, `connectTimeout`, `idle`, `maxDuration`, `sendTimeout` or `ping` is not a positive duration. Or a `protocols` entry is not one word. Or the server did not open a socket. It sent a redirect, which is never followed, and the message names its `Location`. Or it sent a status other than `101`. Or it chose a subprotocol that `protocols` did not offer.
