### `Core\Http\Response`

Keywords: status, text, bytes, jsonAs, header, headers, tls

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Http\Response->status`](#core-core-http-response-status) | `status(): int` |
| [`Core\Http\Response->text`](#core-core-http-response-text) | `text(): tainted string` |
| [`Core\Http\Response->bytes`](#core-core-http-response-bytes) | `bytes(): tainted bytes` |
| [`Core\Http\Response->jsonAs`](#core-core-http-response-jsonas) | `jsonAs<T>({ maxDepth?: uint }): T` |
| [`Core\Http\Response->header`](#core-core-http-response-header) | `header(string $name): ?tainted string` |
| [`Core\Http\Response->headers`](#core-core-http-response-headers) | `headers(string $name): array<tainted string>` |
| [`Core\Http\Response->tls`](#core-core-http-response-tls) | `tls(): ?Core\Http\TlsInfo` |

<a id="core-core-http-response-status"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Response->status`

```nvs skip
$response->status(): int
```

Returns the reply's HTTP status code, exactly as the server sent it.

**Returns** `int` — The three-digit code from the status line. A `404` or a `500` is a normal reply and is returned here. Only a request that gets no reply at all throws an error.

<a id="core-core-http-response-text"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Response->text`

```nvs skip
$response->text(): tainted string
```

Returns the reply's body as text.

**Returns** `tainted string` — The body, as a `tainted` string. Another server chose these bytes. The approved address tells you where they came from, but not what they contain. Each place that does not accept `tainted` text has its own check to clean it. There is no general one.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The body is not valid UTF-8, so it cannot be a `string`. The body is not repaired. A replacement character would change the body, and the program could not tell. `bytes` reads the same body without this check.

<a id="core-core-http-response-bytes"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Response->bytes`

```nvs skip
$response->bytes(): tainted bytes
```

Returns the reply's body as the bytes that arrived. Use it for replies that are not text, such as an image, an archive or a signature.

**Returns** `tainted bytes` — Every byte of the body. It is `tainted`, for the same reason as `text`. The bytes are not checked. A reply that is not UTF-8 is returned here, but `text` throws an error for it.

<a id="core-core-http-response-jsonas"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Response->jsonAs`

```nvs skip
$response->jsonAs<T>({ maxDepth?: uint }): T
```

Decodes the reply's body as JSON into an instance of `T`. It works like `Core\Json::decodeAs` on the bytes that `bytes` returns, with the same `{maxDepth?}` options. Write `array<T>` to read a JSON array as one instance per element.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `{ maxDepth: … }` | `uint` (default `512`) | How deep the document may nest. A deeper document throws an error. A scalar document is depth 1. |

**Returns** `T` — A new `T` built from the document's fields, or one `T` per element for an `array<T>`. Every text property of `T` must be declared `tainted`, because another server chose these bytes.

**Throws** `LogicError` — `T` has no `#[Json\Derive]` decoder. Or `maxDepth` is outside 1..=1024.; `ParseError` — The body is not one complete JSON document within that depth. A reply with no body, or a body that is not UTF-8, also throws this error. Or the document is not the object `T` decodes from, or its fields are missing or have the wrong type. Each failed field is one issue on the error, with its own path. The reply's `Content-Type` header is not checked.

<a id="core-core-http-response-header"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Response->header`

```nvs skip
$response->header(string $name): ?tainted string
```

Returns one header of the reply. The name matches in upper or lower case, whichever the server used.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The header name. Upper and lower case are treated the same, as RFC 9110 § 5.1 defines. |

**Returns** `?tainted string` — The header's value, as a `tainted` string. If the server sent the header more than once, the values are joined with `, ` in the order they arrived. The result is `null` if the reply has no such header.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The name is `Set-Cookie`. Two cookies joined into one string are not valid cookies, so this method does not join them. Use `headers` to read `Set-Cookie`.

<a id="core-core-http-response-headers"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Response->headers`

```nvs skip
$response->headers(string $name): array<tainted string>
```

Returns every value the reply sent under one header name, as separate entries. Use it when the joined value from `header` is not enough. It is the only way to read `Set-Cookie`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The header name. Upper and lower case are treated the same, as in `header`. |

**Returns** `array<tainted string>` — One `tainted` entry per header line, in the order they arrived. The result is an empty array if the reply has no such header. A header sent once gives an array with one entry.

<a id="core-core-http-response-tls"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Response->tls`

```nvs skip
$response->tls(): ?Core\Http\TlsInfo
```

Returns the details of the TLS connection this reply came over. They include the settings both sides agreed on, and whether the server's certificate was checked.

**Returns** `?Core\Http\TlsInfo` — The TLS details. The result is `null` if the reply did not use TLS. That is the case for a plain `http` call, or for a call that a test served from its table of replies.

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo"></a>
### `Core\Http\TlsInfo`

Keywords: version, cipher, verified, peerChain, subject, issuer, expiry

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Http\TlsInfo->version`](#core-core-http-tlsinfo-version) | `version(): string` |
| [`Core\Http\TlsInfo->cipher`](#core-core-http-tlsinfo-cipher) | `cipher(): string` |
| [`Core\Http\TlsInfo->verified`](#core-core-http-tlsinfo-verified) | `verified(): bool` |
| [`Core\Http\TlsInfo->peerChain`](#core-core-http-tlsinfo-peerchain) | `peerChain(): array<tainted string>` |
| [`Core\Http\TlsInfo->subject`](#core-core-http-tlsinfo-subject) | `subject(): tainted string` |
| [`Core\Http\TlsInfo->issuer`](#core-core-http-tlsinfo-issuer) | `issuer(): tainted string` |
| [`Core\Http\TlsInfo->expiry`](#core-core-http-tlsinfo-expiry) | `expiry(): Core\Time\Instant` |

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo-version"></a>
#### `Core\Http\TlsInfo->version`

```nvs skip
$tlsInfo->version(): string
```

Returns the TLS version that both sides agreed on.

**Returns** `string` — `TLSv1.3` or `TLSv1.2`, the way TLS tools print it. For a version that this build cannot name, the result is the version's `0x` code from the registry.

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo-cipher"></a>
#### `Core\Http\TlsInfo->cipher`

```nvs skip
$tlsInfo->cipher(): string
```

Returns the cipher suite that both sides agreed on, by its IANA registry name.

**Returns** `string` — A name such as `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`. If the registry has no name for the suite, the result is its `0x` code.

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo-verified"></a>
#### `Core\Http\TlsInfo->verified`

```nvs skip
$tlsInfo->verified(): bool
```

Returns whether the connection checked both the server's certificate chain and the name on it.

**Returns** `bool` — `true` if the chain was checked up to a trusted root, and the URL's host matched the certificate. The trusted roots are the configured `roots` or the call's own `tlsCa`. `false` if the call skipped either check. A call can skip a check only if a `[capabilities.tls]` grant lists the host.

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo-peerchain"></a>
#### `Core\Http\TlsInfo->peerChain`

```nvs skip
$tlsInfo->peerChain(): array<tainted string>
```

Returns the certificate chain the server sent, as PEM, leaf first.

**Returns** `array<tainted string>` — One PEM block per certificate, leaf first. The result is an empty array if the server sent none. Every entry is `tainted`, because the server chose these bytes.

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo-subject"></a>
#### `Core\Http\TlsInfo->subject`

```nvs skip
$tlsInfo->subject(): tainted string
```

Returns the subject of the leaf certificate, written as an RFC 4514 distinguished name.

**Returns** `tainted string` — The same text that `openssl x509 -subject` prints, such as `CN=api.example.com`. It is `tainted`, for the same reason as `peerChain`.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The server sent no certificate, or its leaf certificate is not X.509 that this method can read. `version`, `cipher`, `verified` and `peerChain` still work, because they do not read inside a certificate.

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo-issuer"></a>
#### `Core\Http\TlsInfo->issuer`

```nvs skip
$tlsInfo->issuer(): tainted string
```

Returns the issuer of the leaf certificate, written as an RFC 4514 distinguished name.

**Returns** `tainted string` — Who signed the leaf certificate, in the same format as `subject`. It is `tainted` for the same reason.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The server sent no certificate, or its leaf certificate is not X.509 that this method can read. `version`, `cipher`, `verified` and `peerChain` still work, because they do not read inside a certificate.

<a id="core-core-http-tlsinfo-expiry"></a>
#### `Core\Http\TlsInfo->expiry`

```nvs skip
$tlsInfo->expiry(): Core\Time\Instant
```

Returns when the leaf certificate stops being valid. This is its `notAfter` field.

**Returns** `Core\Time\Instant` — The instant when the server's certificate expires. Operators often want a program to check this for the services it calls.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The server sent no certificate, or its leaf certificate is not X.509 that this method can read. `version`, `cipher`, `verified` and `peerChain` still work, because they do not read inside a certificate.; `RuntimeError` — The certificate has no end date. Its `notAfter` is `9999-12-31`, which is later than the last `Core\Time\Instant`.

<a id="core-core-http-socket"></a>
### `Core\Http\Socket`

Keywords: receive, send, sendBytes, close, protocol

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Http\Socket->receive`](#core-core-http-socket-receive) | `receive(): ?Core\Socket\Message` |
| [`Core\Http\Socket->send`](#core-core-http-socket-send) | `send(string $frame): void` |
| [`Core\Http\Socket->sendBytes`](#core-core-http-socket-sendbytes) | `sendBytes(bytes $frame): void` |
| [`Core\Http\Socket->close`](#core-core-http-socket-close) | `close(?uint $code = null, ?string $reason = null): void` |
| [`Core\Http\Socket->protocol`](#core-core-http-socket-protocol) | `protocol(): ?string` |

<a id="core-core-http-socket-receive"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Socket->receive`

```nvs skip
$socket->receive(): ?Core\Socket\Message
```

Waits for the next message from the peer and returns it. When the connection is closed, it returns `null`.

**Returns** `?Core\Socket\Message` — A `Core\Socket\Message`. Its `text()` or `bytes()` returns the content, which is `tainted` because it comes from the network. Its `topic()` and `value()` are `null`, because only a message from another isolate sets them. `null` means the connection is closed, by the peer or by your program.

**Throws** `TimeoutError` — The peer sent nothing for longer than `idle`, or the socket's `maxDuration` ended while this call was waiting. A peer that sends only pings is not silent, so only `maxDuration` limits it.; `IOError` — The connection failed while this call was waiting for a message.; `RuntimeError` — The peer sent a message larger than `maxMessage`. The socket is closed with code `1009` before the error is thrown. This stops the peer from filling the task's memory with a message that nobody reads.; `LogicError` — Another `receive()` is already waiting on this socket. Each message goes to one receiver, so only the task that owns the socket reads from it.

<a id="core-core-http-socket-send"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Socket->send`

```nvs skip
$socket->send(string $frame): void
```

Sends one text message to the peer.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$frame` | `string` (neutral) | The text to send, as one RFC 6455 text message, however many frames it needs. A `tainted` value is allowed. Text your program sends to another server cannot run as code on your side. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The socket is closed, so the message cannot be sent.; `TimeoutError` — The frame was not written before `sendTimeout` ended. This usually means the peer has stopped reading. It is also thrown when the socket's `maxDuration` ends first.; `IOError` — The connection failed while the frame was going out.

<a id="core-core-http-socket-sendbytes"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Socket->sendBytes`

```nvs skip
$socket->sendBytes(bytes $frame): void
```

Sends one binary message to the peer. `send` sends a text message.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$frame` | `bytes` (neutral) | The bytes to send, as one binary message. A `tainted` value is allowed, as it is for `send`. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The socket is closed, so the message cannot be sent.; `TimeoutError` — The frame was not written before `sendTimeout` ended. This usually means the peer has stopped reading. It is also thrown when the socket's `maxDuration` ends first.; `IOError` — The connection failed while the frame was going out.

<a id="core-core-http-socket-close"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Socket->close`

```nvs skip
$socket->close(?uint $code = null, ?string $reason = null): void
```

Closes the connection. It sends the close frame and waits for the peer's close frame, up to `sendTimeout`. Then it frees the connection.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$code` | `?uint` (default `null`) | The close code to send. If you leave it out, it is `1000`, a normal close. |
| `$reason` | `?string` (default `null`, neutral) | Text to send with the code, for a peer that logs it. If you leave it out, no text is sent. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. If the peer never sends its close frame, the connection is closed anyway, without an error. So a normal close needs no `catch`. Closing a socket that is already closed does nothing.

<a id="core-core-http-socket-protocol"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Socket->protocol`

```nvs skip
$socket->protocol(): ?string
```

Returns the subprotocol that the opening handshake chose, from the ones in `protocols`.

**Returns** `?string` — The name the peer chose. It is `null` if the call offered no protocol or the peer chose none. If the peer chooses a name that was not offered, the handshake fails and no socket is returned.

<a id="core-core-http-stream"></a>
### `Core\Http\Stream`

Keywords: status, header, headers, events, lines, chunks, saveTo

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Http\Stream->status`](#core-core-http-stream-status) | `status(): int` |
| [`Core\Http\Stream->header`](#core-core-http-stream-header) | `header(string $name): ?tainted string` |
| [`Core\Http\Stream->headers`](#core-core-http-stream-headers) | `headers(string $name): array<tainted string>` |
| [`Core\Http\Stream->events`](#core-core-http-stream-events) | `events(): Core\Http\Events` |
| [`Core\Http\Stream->lines`](#core-core-http-stream-lines) | `lines(): Core\Http\Lines` |
| [`Core\Http\Stream->chunks`](#core-core-http-stream-chunks) | `chunks(): Core\Http\Chunks` |
| [`Core\Http\Stream->saveTo`](#core-core-http-stream-saveto) | `saveTo(string $path, uint $max): void` |

<a id="core-core-http-stream-status"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Stream->status`

```nvs skip
$stream->status(): int
```

Returns the status code of the reply. It works before the body is read.

**Returns** `int` — The three-digit status code, as an `int`. A `4xx` or `5xx` code is returned like any other code. It does not throw an error.

<a id="core-core-http-stream-header"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Stream->header`

```nvs skip
$stream->header(string $name): ?tainted string
```

Returns one header of the reply, by name. When the server sent the header more than once, the values are joined into one, as RFC 9110 § 5.3 allows.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The header name. Upper and lower case do not matter. |

**Returns** `?tainted string` — The header value, or `null` when the reply has no such header. The value is `tainted`, which means it came from outside your program, like every byte of a reply.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The name is `Set-Cookie`. Its values cannot be joined, so use `headers` to read them.

<a id="core-core-http-stream-headers"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Stream->headers`

```nvs skip
$stream->headers(string $name): array<tainted string>
```

Returns every value of one header of the reply, as separate items. `header` joins the same values into one string.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The header name. Upper and lower case do not matter. |

**Returns** `array<tainted string>` — The values in the order they arrived, each `tainted`. A header that arrived once gives a list of one value. A header that never arrived gives an empty list.

<a id="core-core-http-stream-events"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Stream->events`

```nvs skip
$stream->events(): Core\Http\Events
```

Reads the body as server-sent events, in the WHATWG EventSource format. Use it for a `text/event-stream` reply.

**Returns** `Core\Http\Events` — An `Iterable<Core\Http\Event>` that a `foreach` can loop over once. An event is complete at the blank line that ends it. A comment line is skipped. A `retry` line is read and ignored, because your program decides when to reconnect.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The body of this stream has already been read. A body can be read only once, in one way. The error message names the method that read it.; `RuntimeError` — A line of the reply is longer than the line limit, or the `data` of one event is longer than the event limit. Both limits are fixed, so a server cannot make your program use unlimited memory.

<a id="core-core-http-stream-lines"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Stream->lines`

```nvs skip
$stream->lines(): Core\Http\Lines
```

Reads the body one line at a time. Use it for a reply that sends text line by line, such as JSON Lines.

**Returns** `Core\Http\Lines` — An `Iterable<tainted string>` that a `foreach` can loop over once. A line ends at `\n`, and a `\r` at the end of a line is removed. The last line does not need a `\n`.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The body of this stream has already been read. The error message names the method that read it.; `RuntimeError` — A line of the reply is longer than the line limit.

<a id="core-core-http-stream-chunks"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Stream->chunks`

```nvs skip
$stream->chunks(): Core\Http\Chunks
```

Reads the body as raw bytes, in pieces. Use it for a reply whose bytes have a format of their own.

**Returns** `Core\Http\Chunks` — An `Iterable<tainted bytes>` that a `foreach` can loop over once. The size of each piece depends on the network and has no meaning, so you cannot choose a size. If you need blocks of a fixed size, collect the bytes yourself.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The body of this stream has already been read. The error message names the method that read it.

<a id="core-core-http-stream-saveto"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Stream->saveTo`

```nvs skip
$stream->saveTo(string $path, uint $max): void
```

Writes the body directly to the file at `$path`. Only one piece of the body is in memory at a time. Needs the `fs.write` capability for the path. It uses `Core\IO::writeStream` to write the file.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$path` | `string` (sink) | The file to write. Nothing may exist at the path yet. This method cannot replace a file. The `overwrite` option of `Core\IO::writeStream` can. |
| `$max` | `uint` | The largest number of bytes to accept. It is required, because the server chooses the length of the reply, and the bytes use disk space. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. When writing fails part of the way through, the partial file is deleted before the error is thrown. So nobody later finds an incomplete file.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The body of this stream has already been read. The error message names the method that read it.; `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not allow `fs.write` for this path, or the body is longer than `max` bytes.; `IOError` — Something is already at the path, or the operating system could not create or write the file.

<a id="core-core-http-event"></a>
### `Core\Http\Event`

Keywords: data, name, id

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Http\Event->data`](#core-core-http-event-data) | `data(): tainted string` |

<a id="core-core-http-event-data"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Event->data`

```nvs skip
$event->data(): tainted string
```

Returns the data of this event. Every `data` line of the event is joined with a newline, and the last newline is removed.

**Returns** `tainted string` — The data, `tainted` like every byte of a reply. An event with no `data` line is not given to the loop at all.

<a id="core-core-http-event-name"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Event->name`

```nvs skip
$event->name(): ?tainted string
```

Returns the type of this event. The server sends it as an `event` line.

**Returns** `?tainted string` — The name, `tainted`. It is `null` when the event has no `event` line. The format calls such an event a `message`.

<a id="core-core-http-event-id"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Event->id`

```nvs skip
$event->id(): ?tainted string
```

Returns the last event id the server set. A program that resumes a stream sends it back in the `Last-Event-ID` header.

**Returns** `?tainted string` — The id, `tainted`, or `null` when no id was set. The format ignores an id that contains a NUL byte, so the result is `null`.

<a id="core-core-http-part"></a>
### `Core\Http\Part`

Keywords: file, bytes

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Http\Part::file`](#core-core-http-part-file) | `file(string $path, { filename?: string, contentType?: string }): Core\Http\Part` |
| [`Core\Http\Part::bytes`](#core-core-http-part-bytes) | `bytes(secret tainted string\|secret tainted bytes $data, string $filename, { contentType?: string }): Core\Http\Part` |

<a id="core-core-http-part-file"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Part::file`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Part::file(string $path, { filename?: string, contentType?: string }): Core\Http\Part
```

Creates a body, or one field of a multipart body, from the file at `$path`. The file is read while the request is sent, so it is not loaded into memory first. It needs the `fs.read` capability. The capability is checked at this call, so a path without access throws an error here.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$path` | `string` (sink) | The file to send. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it. |
| `{ filename: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The file name sent to the server. By default, it is the last part of the path. |
| `{ contentType: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The media type of this part. If it is not given, a multipart field is sent as `application/octet-stream`. A whole body uses the call's own `contentType`. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Part` — A part. Pass it as `body` or as one key of `multipart`.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not grant `fs.read` for this path.; `IOError` — Nothing exists at `$path`, or the operating system did not return its details.

<a id="core-core-http-part-bytes"></a>
#### `Core\Http\Part::bytes`

```nvs skip
Core\Http\Part::bytes(secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes $data, string $filename, { contentType?: string }): Core\Http\Part
```

Creates a body, or one field of a multipart body, from bytes that are already in memory. You give the data a file name.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$data` | `secret tainted string\|secret tainted bytes` | The bytes to send, as a `string` or a `bytes`. |
| `$filename` | `string` (neutral) | The file name sent to the server. It is required, because the data has no name of its own. |
| `{ contentType: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The media type of this part. The default is the same as for `file`. |

**Returns** `Core\Http\Part` — A part. Pass it as `body` or as one key of `multipart`.

### `Core\Net`

Keywords: connect, listen, bindDatagram, connectLocal, listenLocal

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Net::connect`](#core-core-net-connect) | `connect(string $host, uint $port, Core\Time\Duration $within): Core\Net\Stream` |
| [`Core\Net::listen`](#core-core-net-listen) | `listen(string $address, uint $port): Core\Net\Listener` |

| [`Core\Net::listenLocal`](#core-core-net-listenlocal) | `listenLocal(string $path): Core\Net\Listener` |

<a id="core-core-net-connect"></a>
#### `Core\Net::connect`

```nvs skip
Core\Net::connect(string $host, uint $port, Core\Time\Duration $within): Core\Net\Stream
```

Opens a TCP connection to `$host` on `$port`. While the connection opens, other work keeps running. The configuration must allow the host in `net.connect`. The address of the host must not be in a range that the address policy denies.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$host` | `string` (sink) | A host name or an IP address. It is checked against `net.connect` before its address is looked up. The connection goes to the one address that is found. |
| `$port` | `uint` | The port to connect to, 1 to 65535. |
| `$within` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long opening the connection may take. This limit ends when the connection is open. A later read uses the time limit that you give to that read. |

**Returns** `Core\Net\Stream` — An open `Core\Net\Stream`. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not allow this host in `net.connect`. It is also thrown when the host has no address, or its address is in a denied range. It is also thrown when `$port` is not a valid port, or `$within` is not a positive length of time.; `TimeoutError` — The connection was not open yet when the time in `$within` ended.; `IOError` — The connection failed. The other side refused it, it could not be reached, or it was reset while it opened.

<a id="core-core-net-listen"></a>
#### `Core\Net::listen`

```nvs skip
Core\Net::listen(string $address, uint $port): Core\Net\Listener
```

Opens a TCP socket that listens on `$address` and `$port`. The configuration must allow this exact address and port in `net.listen`. The address policy of `net.connect` does not apply, because its rules are for the hosts you connect to.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$address` | `string` (sink) | An IP address, such as `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `0.0.0.0`. A host name is not allowed. The grant names one address and port, and a host name can have two addresses. |
| `$port` | `uint` | The port to listen on. With `0`, the operating system chooses a port, and `Core\Net\Listener::port` returns it. |

**Returns** `Core\Net\Listener` — A `Core\Net\Listener` that listens. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not allow this address and port in `net.listen`. It is also thrown when `$address` is not an IP address, or `$port` is not a valid port.; `IOError` — The operating system did not allow the socket. The port is already in use, or the address does not belong to this host.

<a id="core-core-net-binddatagram"></a>
#### `Core\Net::bindDatagram`

```nvs skip
Core\Net::bindDatagram(string $address, uint $port): Core\Net\Datagram
```

Opens a UDP socket on `$address` and `$port`. Like a TCP listener, it needs this exact address and port in `net.listen`. Sending to another host needs a separate grant, which `Core\Net\Datagram::send` checks.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$address` | `string` (sink) | An IP address, such as `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `0.0.0.0`. A host name is not allowed, for the same reason as in `Core\Net::listen`: the grant names one address and port. |
| `$port` | `uint` | The port to use. With `0`, the operating system chooses a port, and `Core\Net\Datagram::port` returns it. |

**Returns** `Core\Net\Datagram` — A `Core\Net\Datagram` on that address and port. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not allow this address and port in `net.listen`. It is also thrown when `$address` is not an IP address, or `$port` is not a valid port.; `IOError` — The operating system did not allow the socket. The port is already in use, or the address does not belong to this host.

<a id="core-core-net-connectlocal"></a>
#### `Core\Net::connectLocal`

```nvs skip
Core\Net::connectLocal(string $path, Core\Time\Duration $within): Core\Net\Stream
```

Connects to the Unix-domain socket at `$path`. While the connection opens, other work keeps running. The configuration must allow the path in `net.local`, which is a separate grant. `net.connect` never allows a path, because it has no rules for paths.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$path` | `string` (sink) | The absolute path of a socket that listens. It is never read as a host or as a URL. This is the only method that connects to a path. |
| `$within` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long to wait for the connection. This limit is for this call only. A local connection waits only when the listener's queue of waiting connections is full. |

**Returns** `Core\Net\Stream` — A connected `Core\Net\Stream`. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not allow this path in `net.local`. It is also thrown when this build has no support for Unix-domain sockets, or `$within` is not a positive length of time.; `TimeoutError` — The connection was not open yet when the time in `$within` ended.; `IOError` — The operating system did not allow the path. Nothing listens there, the program has no permission, or the path is too long for the platform.

<a id="core-core-net-listenlocal"></a>
#### `Core\Net::listenLocal`

```nvs skip
Core\Net::listenLocal(string $path): Core\Net\Listener
```

Creates a Unix-domain socket at `$path` and listens on it. The configuration must allow the path in `net.local`. Listening needs this grant too, because any program on this host that finds the socket can connect to it.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$path` | `string` (sink) | The absolute path where the socket is created. Nothing may exist at this path yet. The path is not deleted when the socket closes, because something else may be there by then. |

**Returns** `Core\Net\Listener` — A `Core\Net\Listener` that listens. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends. Its `port()` method throws an error, because a socket at a path has no port.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not allow this path in `net.local`, or this build has no support for Unix-domain sockets.; `IOError` — The operating system did not allow the path. Something already exists at the path, its folder does not exist, or the program has no permission to create it.

<a id="core-core-net-stream"></a>
### `Core\Net\Stream`

Keywords: read, write, close

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Net\Stream->read`](#core-core-net-stream-read) | `read(uint $max, Core\Time\Duration $within): tainted bytes` |
| [`Core\Net\Stream->write`](#core-core-net-stream-write) | `write(bytes $payload, Core\Time\Duration $within): uint` |
| [`Core\Net\Stream->close`](#core-core-net-stream-close) | `close(): void` |

<a id="core-core-net-stream-read"></a>
#### `Core\Net\Stream->read`

```nvs skip
$stream->read(uint $max, Core\Time\Duration $within): tainted bytes
```

Reads the bytes that have arrived, up to `$max` bytes. It waits no longer than `$within`. Fewer bytes than `$max` is normal and not an error, because a socket returns only what has arrived.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$max` | `uint` | The largest number of bytes to return. When `$max` is very large, one read returns fewer bytes, because the buffer has a smaller limit. |
| `$within` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long to wait for the first byte. This limit is for this call only. |

**Returns** `tainted bytes` — The bytes that arrived, as `tainted bytes`. When the other side has closed its half of the connection, the result is an empty `bytes`. This is how you see the end of the stream.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — This handle is closed, or `$within` is not a positive length of time.; `TimeoutError` — Nothing arrived within `$within`.; `IOError` — The connection failed. The other side reset it, or the network lost it.

<a id="core-core-net-stream-write"></a>
#### `Core\Net\Stream->write`

```nvs skip
$stream->write(bytes $payload, Core\Time\Duration $within): uint
```

Writes `$payload` to the other side, and waits no longer than `$within`. It returns how many bytes the socket accepted. The socket may accept only some of the bytes. This is normal, and your program then sends the rest.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$payload` | `bytes` (neutral) | The bytes to send. |
| `$within` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long to wait until the socket accepts bytes. This limit is for this call only. |

**Returns** `uint` — How many bytes of `$payload` were written. It is between `0` and the length of `$payload`.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — This handle is closed, or `$within` is not a positive length of time.; `TimeoutError` — The socket accepted nothing within `$within`.; `IOError` — The connection failed. The other side reset it, or closed its half for reading.

<a id="core-core-net-stream-close"></a>
#### `Core\Net\Stream->close`

```nvs skip
$stream->close(): void
```

Closes this connection and frees the resources it uses. When a request ends, it closes every socket that it opened and did not close.

**Returns** `void` — Nothing.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — This handle is already closed.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |

| `$within` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long to wait for a client. It is the limit for this call only. |

<a id="core-core-net-listener-close"></a>


Stops listening and frees the port. Connections that were already accepted stay open, because each one is a separate socket.

### `Core\Net\Datagram`

Keywords: send, receive, port, close

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Net\Datagram->send`](#core-core-net-datagram-send) | `send(string $host, uint $port, bytes $payload, Core\Time\Duration $within): uint` |

| [`Core\Net\Datagram->close`](#core-core-net-datagram-close) | `close(): void` |

<a id="core-core-net-datagram-send"></a>
#### `Core\Net\Datagram->send`

```nvs skip
$datagram->send(string $host, uint $port, bytes $payload, Core\Time\Duration $within): uint
```

Sends one message to `$host` on `$port`, and returns how many bytes were sent. The configuration must allow the host in `net.connect`. The address of the host must not be in a range that the address policy denies. These are the same checks as for a TCP connection.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$host` | `string` (sink) | A host name or an IP address. It is checked against `net.connect` before its address is looked up. The message goes to the one address that is found. |
| `$port` | `uint` | The port to send to, 1 to 65535. |
| `$payload` | `bytes` (neutral) | The bytes of one message. A message is never sent in parts. A message that is too large for the network throws an error and is not split. |
| `$within` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long to wait until the socket accepts the message. This limit is for this call only. |

**Returns** `uint` — How many bytes were sent. When the call succeeds, this is always the length of `$payload`.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration does not allow this host in `net.connect`. It is also thrown when the host has no address, or its address is in a denied range. It is also thrown when `$port` is not a valid port, this handle is closed, or `$within` is not a positive length of time.; `TimeoutError` — The socket did not accept the message within `$within`.; `IOError` — The operating system did not allow the send. The message is larger than the maximum size, or the network cannot be reached.

<a id="core-core-net-datagram-receive"></a>
#### `Core\Net\Datagram->receive`

```nvs skip
$datagram->receive(uint $max, Core\Time\Duration $within): Core\Net\Datagram\Message
```

Waits for one message, no longer than `$within`. It returns the message and the address that sent it. It needs no grant, because `net.listen` was checked when this socket was opened. Your program does not choose who sends to it.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$max` | `uint` | How many bytes to keep. The limit is 64 KiB, because no message is larger. A message arrives whole or not at all. If it is longer than `$max`, only the first `$max` bytes are kept, and the rest is lost. No later call returns the rest. |
| `$within` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long to wait for a message. This limit is for this call only. |

**Returns** `Core\Net\Datagram\Message` — A `Core\Net\Datagram\Message` with the bytes, and the address and port they came from.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — This handle is closed, or `$within` is not a positive length of time.; `TimeoutError` — No datagram arrived within `$within`.; `IOError` — The operating system could not receive. On Windows, this error also reports that an earlier send from this socket could not reach its address.

<a id="core-core-net-datagram-port"></a>
#### `Core\Net\Datagram->port`

```nvs skip
$datagram->port(): uint
```

Returns the port this socket uses. If your program asked for port `0`, this is the port that the operating system chose.

**Returns** `uint` — The port, from 1 to 65535.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — This handle is closed.; `IOError` — The operating system did not return the port of this socket.

<a id="core-core-net-datagram-close"></a>
#### `Core\Net\Datagram->close`

```nvs skip
$datagram->close(): void
```

Closes this socket, and frees its port and the resources it uses. When a request ends, it closes every socket that it opened and did not close.

**Returns** `void` — Nothing.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — This handle is already closed.

<a id="core-core-cache"></a>
### `Core\Cache`

Keywords: cache, memoize, in-memory cache, per-process, redis, ttl, expiry, hit, miss, cross-request state, which cache, memory, shared

`Core\Cache` keeps a value after the request that made it ends. It has two caches, and both return a
`Core\Cache\Store` with the same methods: `put`, `get`, `forget`, `putSecret` and `getSecret`.

**`Core\Cache::memory()` keeps values in the memory of this server process.** Every core of one
`nvs serve`, or the one `nvs run`, sees the same values. It needs no configuration and no network,
so it is fast. A restart empties it, and a second server process or machine does not see it. Use it
for ordinary caching: a slow result, a parsed template, a table that many requests read.

**`Core\Cache::shared()` is a store on the network,** such as Redis, at the `[cache.shared] url` the
person who runs the server sets. Every process on every machine sees the same values, and they stay
after a restart. Use it when another server must find the value, or when your program would be
wrong if the value were missing: a session, a lock, a quota.

The memory cache has a size limit, `[cache.memory] max_size`. When it is full, it forgets the value
written longest ago, and `put` does not fail. On both caches any `get` may return `null`, so your
program must be able to build the value again. `put` copies the value into the cache, and `get`
returns a copy.

```nvs
<?nvs
var $cache = Core\Cache::memory();
echo $cache->get('greeting') ?? 'not in the cache', "\n";

// Every request on this server can now read this value.
$cache->put('greeting', 'hello', { ttl: 30s });
echo $cache->get('greeting') ?? 'not in the cache', "\n";

$cache->forget('greeting');
echo $cache->get('greeting') ?? 'forgotten', "\n";
```
```output
not in the cache
hello
forgotten
```

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Cache::memory`](#core-core-cache-memory) | `memory(): Core\Cache\Store` |
| [`Core\Cache::shared`](#core-core-cache-shared) | `shared(): Core\Cache\Store` |

<a id="core-core-cache-memory"></a>
#### `Core\Cache::memory`

```nvs skip
Core\Cache::memory(): Core\Cache\Store
```

Returns the cache in the memory of this server process. Every request this process serves reads the same entries. The cache is empty again when the process stops. Use it for ordinary application caching.

**Returns** `Core\Cache\Store` — A `Core\Cache\Store` for the entries of this process. Every request this process serves can read them. An entry can be missing at any time. The cache deletes old entries to stay under its size limit, and another server process has its own entries. If your program is wrong when `get` returns `null`, use `shared` instead.

<a id="core-core-cache-shared"></a>
#### `Core\Cache::shared`

```nvs skip
Core\Cache::shared(): Core\Cache\Store
```

Returns the cache in the external store that `[cache.shared] url` names. Every server process and every machine that uses this store reads the same entries.

**Returns** `Core\Cache\Store` — A `Core\Cache\Store` for the configured shared store. Every server process that uses the store reads the same entries.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The program does not have the capability `cache.shared`. Or no `[cache.shared] url` is set, or the client cannot read that URL. Each of these is a missing setting, not a failed store.; `IOError` — The configured store cannot be reached. The call throws this error. It does not return `null`, because a missing entry and a failed store mean different things.

<a id="core-core-cache-store"></a>
### `Core\Cache\Store`

Keywords: put, get, forget, putSecret, getSecret

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Cache\Store->put`](#core-core-cache-store-put) | `put(string $key, mixed $value, { ttl?: Core\Time\Duration }): void` |
| [`Core\Cache\Store->get`](#core-core-cache-store-get) | `get(string $key): mixed` |
| [`Core\Cache\Store->forget`](#core-core-cache-store-forget) | `forget(string $key): void` |
| [`Core\Cache\Store->putSecret`](#core-core-cache-store-putsecret) | `putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Core\Time\Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys): void` |
| [`Core\Cache\Store->getSecret`](#core-core-cache-store-getsecret) | `getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, { fill?: callable(): Core\Cache\SecretEntry, wait?: Core\Time\Duration }): ?secret string` |

<a id="core-core-cache-store-put"></a>
#### `Core\Cache\Store->put`

```nvs skip
$store->put(string $key, mixed $value, { ttl?: Core\Time\Duration }): void
```

Saves a copy of `$value` in the store under `$key`. It replaces any value already there. The copy is deep, so the entry shares nothing with the request that wrote it.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$key` | `string` (neutral) | The name to store under. A `tainted` string is allowed, because the key is never part of a returned value. |
| `$value` | `mixed` | The value to copy in. It cannot be a callable or a `secret`. The same rule applies to a value sent to an isolate. |
| `{ ttl: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | How long the entry stays readable, counted from this call. Without it, the entry stays until the cache deletes it to stay under its size limit, or until another `put` replaces it. A `ttl` of zero or less deletes the entry under the key and stores nothing. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. A later `get` can still return `null`, because an entry can be deleted at any time.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The value cannot be stored. It is or contains a callable, or an object with a `secret` property that was not revealed.; `IOError` — Only on a `shared` cache: the store cannot be reached, or it does not accept the write.

<a id="core-core-cache-store-get"></a>
#### `Core\Cache\Store->get`

```nvs skip
$store->get(string $key): mixed
```

Returns a copy of the entry stored under `$key`. If there is no entry, it returns `null`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$key` | `string` (neutral) | The name to read. A `tainted` string is allowed, as on `put`. |

**Returns** `mixed` — The value as it was copied in, or `null` when there is no entry. An entry can be missing at any time, so your program has to handle `null`.

**Throws** `ParseError` — The entry contains a class that this program does not have. `Core\Serialize::decode` throws the same error. This happens when a new version of the program changes its classes but the store keeps old entries.; `IOError` — Only on a `shared` cache: the store cannot be reached. A missing entry returns `null` on both caches and is not an error.

<a id="core-core-cache-store-forget"></a>
#### `Core\Cache\Store->forget`

```nvs skip
$store->forget(string $key): void
```

Deletes the entry under `$key` from this store. It works whether or not there is an entry.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$key` | `string` (neutral) | The name to delete. A `tainted` string is allowed, as on `put`. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. If there is no entry under the key, the call does nothing. An entry can be missing at any time, so the call does not tell you whether there was one.

**Throws** `IOError` — Only on a `shared` cache: the store cannot be reached, or it does not accept the command.

<a id="core-core-cache-store-putsecret"></a>
#### `Core\Cache\Store->putSecret`

```nvs skip
$store->putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Core\Time\Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys): void
```

Encrypts `$value` with the newest key in `$keys` and stores the encrypted bytes under `$key`. This is the only way to put a secret in a cache. The cache never contains the unencrypted value.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$key` | `string` (neutral) | The name to store under. A `tainted` string is allowed, as on `put`. The name is part of the encrypted entry. If the entry is moved to another name, it cannot be decrypted. |
| `$value` | `secret string` (neutral) | The secret to store. A plain `string` is also accepted. The call does not change whether a value is secret. Only the type of the value decides that. |
| `$ttl` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long the secret stays readable, counted from this call. It is required. The lifetime is also stored inside the encrypted entry, so a copy of the entry written back later still expires at the same time. |
| `$keys` | `array<secret bytes>` | The list of keys, newest first, in the same format as for `Core\SignedCookie`. The newest key encrypts. Every key in the list can decrypt. After you add a new key, entries written with an older key in the list can still be read. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. Code that knows the entry's name but not the keys cannot read it. A changed, moved or replayed entry reads as missing. **This does not protect a secret from a compromised process**, because the keys are in the same memory.

**Throws** `LogicError` — `$keys` is empty, or one of its keys does not have the required length. This is a bug in the program, so it throws an error and is not treated as missing.; `IOError` — Only on a `shared` cache: the store cannot be reached, or it does not accept the write.

<a id="core-core-cache-store-getsecret"></a>
#### `Core\Cache\Store->getSecret`

```nvs skip
$store->getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, { fill?: callable(): Core\Cache\SecretEntry, wait?: Core\Time\Duration }): ?secret string
```

Decrypts the secret stored under `$key`, trying every key in `$keys`. If no key can decrypt it, the result is `null`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$key` | `string` (neutral) | The name to read. Use the same name as in `putSecret`, because the name is part of the encrypted entry. |
| `$keys` | `array<secret bytes>` | The list of keys, newest first. Every key is tried. After you add a new key, an entry encrypted with an older key in the list can still be read. |
| `{ fill: … }` | `callable(): Core\Cache\SecretEntry` (default `null`) | A callable that runs when the entry is missing. It returns a `Core\Cache\SecretEntry` with the secret and how long it stays valid. Only one caller in this process runs it, while the others wait. It runs in that caller's request, with that caller's capabilities. If `fill` throws, the waiting callers get no value, and the next caller runs `fill` again. An error in one request never reaches another request. |
| `{ wait: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | How long this caller waits for another caller's `fill`. The default is `[cache.memory] fill_wait`. You cannot wait forever. |

**Returns** `?secret string` — The secret, or `null`. An entry that no key in `$keys` can decrypt returns `null`. An expired entry also returns `null`. Neither is an error, so after a key change the secret is fetched again. A plain `get` on the same name also returns `null`, because `getSecret` is the only way to read a secret.

**Throws** `LogicError` — `$keys` is empty, or one of its keys does not have the required length, as on `putSecret`. It is also thrown when `fill` reads the same key it is filling, because that call would wait for itself.; `TimeoutError` — Another caller in this process was still running `fill` when this call's `wait` was up, which defaults to `[cache.memory] fill_wait`.; `IOError` — Only on a `shared` cache: the store cannot be reached. A missing entry returns `null`, as on `get`.

<a id="core-core-cache-secretentry"></a>
### `Core\Cache\SecretEntry`

Keywords: of

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Cache\SecretEntry::of`](#core-core-cache-secretentry-of) | `of(secret string $value, Core\Time\Duration $ttl): Core\Cache\SecretEntry` |

<a id="core-core-cache-secretentry-of"></a>
#### `Core\Cache\SecretEntry::of`

```nvs skip
Core\Cache\SecretEntry::of(secret string $value, Core\Time\Duration $ttl): Core\Cache\SecretEntry
```

Creates the entry that a `getSecret` fill returns. It contains the secret that the fill fetched, and how long that secret stays valid.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$value` | `secret string` (neutral) | The secret to store. A plain `string` is also accepted. The call does not change whether a value is secret. Only the type of the value decides that. |
| `$ttl` | `Core\Time\Duration` | How long the entry stays readable, counted from the moment it is stored. Use the lifetime that the source of the secret gives, such as a token's expiry. |

**Returns** `Core\Cache\SecretEntry` — The entry. It has no methods to read the secret or the lifetime. A fill returns it, and your program reads the secret with `getSecret`.

<a id="core-core-ratelimit"></a>
### `Core\RateLimit`

Keywords: consume, shed

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\RateLimit::consume`](#core-core-ratelimit-consume) | `consume(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, { burst?: uint, cost?: uint }): Core\RateLimit\Decision` |
| [`Core\RateLimit::shed`](#core-core-ratelimit-shed) | `shed(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, { burst?: uint, cost?: uint }): Core\RateLimit\Decision` |

<a id="core-core-ratelimit-consume"></a>
#### `Core\RateLimit::consume`

```nvs skip
Core\RateLimit::consume(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, { burst?: uint, cost?: uint }): Core\RateLimit\Decision
```

Charges `$cost` units against the allowance of `$key`, which is `$limit` per `$per`. The count is kept in the shared store. The result says if this call is inside the limit.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$key` | `string` (neutral) | Who the limit is for, such as an account, a tenant or an API key id. A `tainted` value is allowed. A `secret` value is not allowed, because the key is written to the store. Use `Core\Hash::of` of the secret instead. |
| `$limit` | `uint` | How many units are allowed in each `$per`. This is the average rate. It is not a limit on one single moment. |
| `$per` | `Core\Time\Duration` | The period in which `$limit` units are allowed. |
| `{ burst: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | How many units may arrive at the same moment. The default is `$limit`, which allows a whole period's units at once. |
| `{ cost: … }` | `uint` (default `1`) | How many units this call uses. The default is 1. An expensive endpoint can use five units of the same limit, for example. |

**Returns** `Core\RateLimit\Decision` — A `Core\RateLimit\Decision`. Its `retryAfter` is `null` when the call is allowed. Otherwise it is the exact time to wait until the call would be allowed. It is not an estimate, and it is not rounded up to the next period.

**Throws** `IOError` — The shared store cannot be reached, or it rejected the command. The call is never treated as allowed. Your code catches this error and decides whether to allow the call or not.; `RuntimeError` — No `[cache.shared] url` is configured, or `cache.shared` is not granted. This is a deployment mistake, so it is not an `IOError` that your `catch` for a store failure handles. This error is also thrown when `$limit`, `$per` or `$burst` is zero. It is also thrown when the period is too short to divide into `$limit` units, or when `$cost` is larger than `$burst`.

<a id="core-core-ratelimit-shed"></a>
#### `Core\RateLimit::shed`

```nvs skip
Core\RateLimit::shed(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, { burst?: uint, cost?: uint }): Core\RateLimit\Decision
```

Charges `$cost` units against the allowance of `$key`, which is `$limit` per `$per`. The count is kept in the memory of this server process. The result says if this call is inside the limit. Use it to drop load. Use `consume` for a limit you promised to somebody.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$key` | `string` (neutral) | Who the limit is for. A `tainted` value is allowed. A `secret` value is not allowed, the same as for `consume`. |
| `$limit` | `uint` | How many units are allowed in each `$per`, **in this server process**. Every request this process serves counts against the same limit. Two server processes with a limit of 100 allow up to 200, so a number you promised belongs to `consume`. |
| `$per` | `Core\Time\Duration` | The period in which `$limit` units are allowed. |
| `{ burst: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | How many units may arrive at the same moment. The default is `$limit`. |
| `{ cost: … }` | `uint` (default `1`) | How many units this call uses. The default is 1. |

**Returns** `Core\RateLimit\Decision` — A `Core\RateLimit\Decision`. It uses no external store, so it does not throw an `IOError`. The count is kept in the same memory as `Core\Cache::memory()`, which can forget an entry at any time. When a count is forgotten, the key allows a burst again.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — `$limit`, `$per` or `$burst` is zero, the period is too short to divide into `$limit` units, or `$cost` is larger than `$burst`. These are the same errors that `consume` throws.

<a id="core-core-ratelimit-decision-allowed"></a>
#### `Core\RateLimit\Decision->allowed`

```nvs skip
$decision->allowed(): bool
```

Checks whether the call was inside the limit. Only an allowed call is charged.

**Returns** `bool` — `true` when the units were charged. `false` when the call was over the limit and nothing was charged.

<a id="core-core-ratelimit-decision-limit"></a>
#### `Core\RateLimit\Decision->limit`

```nvs skip
$decision->limit(): uint
```

Returns the `$limit` that was used for the decision. You can write a `RateLimit` header from the decision alone.

**Returns** `uint` — The limit as it was passed.

<a id="core-core-ratelimit-decision-remaining"></a>
#### `Core\RateLimit\Decision->remaining`

```nvs skip
$decision->remaining(): uint
```

Returns how many more units are allowed at this moment.

**Returns** `uint` — The units left in the burst, after this call was charged. It is `0` when the next unit has to wait.

<a id="core-core-ratelimit-decision-retryafter"></a>
#### `Core\RateLimit\Decision->retryAfter`

```nvs skip
$decision->retryAfter(): ?Core\Time\Duration
```

Returns how long to wait until the call would be allowed. The time is exact, and it comes from the clock of the store.

**Returns** `?Core\Time\Duration` — `null` when the call is allowed. Otherwise, the `Core\Time\Duration` until the call would be allowed. A `Retry-After` header with this value tells each client its own time to try again. So the rejected clients do not all retry at the same moment.

### `Core\Metrics`

Keywords: increment, observe, gauge

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|

<a id="core-core-metrics-increment"></a>
#### `Core\Metrics::increment`

```nvs skip
Core\Metrics::increment(string $name, { by?: uint, labels?: array<string> }): void
```

Adds to a counter. The first call with `$name` makes that name a counter, and it stays a counter.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (sink) | The series name, `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A `tainted` name does not compile either. |
| `{ by: … }` | `uint` (default `1`) | How much to add. The default is `1`. It cannot be negative, because a counter that goes down looks like a restart of the process. |
| `{ labels: … }` | `array<string>` (default `[]`) | The label values of this series, with the label name as the key. A `tainted` or `secret` value is not allowed. Use an enum case, a value converted with `as`, or a route name. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. A program cannot read a metric back. Only the monitoring system that collects the metrics can read them.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The name is already a different kind of metric, or it already has other label names. The message shows the first call and this one. A new series above the `max_series` limit is **not** an error. Novis does not record it and counts it, and the call returns normally.

<a id="core-core-metrics-observe"></a>
#### `Core\Metrics::observe`

```nvs skip
Core\Metrics::observe(string $name, float $value, { labels?: array<string> }): void
```

Records one measurement in a histogram, such as a duration or a size. The first call with `$name` makes that name a histogram, and it stays a histogram.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (sink) | The series name, `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A `tainted` name does not compile either. |
| `$value` | `float` | The measurement, in the unit of the series. Use seconds for a name that ends in `_seconds`, and bytes for a name that ends in `_bytes`. |
| `{ labels: … }` | `array<string>` (default `[]`) | The label values of this series, with the label name as the key. A `tainted` or `secret` value is not allowed. Use an enum case, a value converted with `as`, or a route name. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. A program cannot read a metric back, the same as with `increment`.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The name is already a different kind of metric, or it already has other label names. The message shows the first call and this one. A new series above the `max_series` limit is **not** an error. Novis does not record it and counts it, and the call returns normally.

<a id="core-core-metrics-gauge"></a>
#### `Core\Metrics::gauge`

```nvs skip
Core\Metrics::gauge(string $name, float $value, { labels?: array<string> }): void
```

Sets a gauge to `$value`. A gauge is a level that goes up and down, such as the number of items waiting. The first call with `$name` makes that name a gauge.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (sink) | The series name, `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A `tainted` name does not compile either. |
| `$value` | `float` | The new value of the gauge. The monitoring system sees the last value set before it collects. |
| `{ labels: … }` | `array<string>` (default `[]`) | The label values of this series, with the label name as the key. A `tainted` or `secret` value is not allowed. Use an enum case, a value converted with `as`, or a route name. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. A program cannot read a metric back, the same as with `increment`.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The name is already a different kind of metric, or it already has other label names. The message shows the first call and this one. A new series above the `max_series` limit is **not** an error. Novis does not record it and counts it, and the call returns normally.

<a id="core-core-reflect-steps"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect::steps`

```nvs skip
Core\Reflect::steps(propertyPath<T> $path): array<Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo>
```

Returns the property that each part of a property path names.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$path` | `propertyPath<T>` | A property path, such as `customer.address.city` of type `propertyPath<Order>`. |

**Returns** `array<Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo>` — One `Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo` for each part of the path, in order. Each one has the property's name, whether it is public, and its declared type. The type shows whether the next part is reached through an object, a nullable object or an array.

**Throws** `LogicError` — `steps` was called through a callable value, so the class the path starts at is not known.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-name"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->name`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->name(): string
```

Returns the name of the described class, with its namespace, as the declaration writes it.

**Returns** `string` — The class name, such as `App\Model\User` for a class in a namespace. It is never an alias that the calling code used.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-properties"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->properties`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->properties(): array<Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo>
```

Returns the properties of the described class, its own and every inherited one. Each has its name, its visibility and its declared type.

**Returns** `array<Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo>` — One `Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo` for each declared property. The properties of every parent class come first, then the class's own. A `private` or `protected` property is in the list, and its `isPublic` returns `false`. `get` checks whether this code may read it.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-readableproperties"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->readableProperties`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->readableProperties(): array<string>
```

Returns the names of the properties that code at this call site may read, in the same order as `properties`. The result depends on where the call is written.

**Returns** `array<string>` — One name for each property that code here may read, without the `$`. Inside the described class, that is every declared property. Anywhere else, it is the `public` ones. `properties` returns the complete list. `get` throws an error here for exactly the properties that are in that list and not in this one.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-hasproperty"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->hasProperty`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->hasProperty(string $name): bool
```

Checks whether the described class declares a property called `$name`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The property's name without the `$`, as the declaration writes it. |

**Returns** `bool` — `true` for a `private` or `protected` property as well as a `public` one. So you can tell a property you may not read from a misspelled name. `properties` tells you whether this code may read it.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-methods"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->methods`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->methods(): array<Core\Reflect\MethodInfo>
```

Returns the methods of the described class, its own and every inherited one. Each has its name, its visibility and the number of parameters it declares.

**Returns** `array<Core\Reflect\MethodInfo>` — One `Core\Reflect\MethodInfo` for each declared method, sorted by name. A method that the calling code may not call is in the list, and its `isPublic()` returns `false`. Listing a method does not call it. `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::call` checks whether this code may call it.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-constants"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->constants`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->constants(): array<Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo>
```

Returns the constants of the described class, its own and every inherited one. Each has its name and its visibility.

**Returns** `array<Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo>` — One `Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo` for each constant of the class, its own declarations first. A constant that a subclass declares again appears once, with the declaration the class uses. The values are not in the list. Use `constant` to read a value, which checks whether this code may read it.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-constant"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->constant`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->constant(string $name): mixed
```

Returns the value of the class constant `$name`. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The constant's name, as the declaration writes it, with no class name and no `::`. |

**Returns** `mixed` — The value, computed at compile time. It is a `string`, `int`, `bool` or `float`, the same type as the value in the declaration.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — Code at this call site may not read the constant `$name`. Reflection has the same visibility rules as ordinary code. This error is also thrown everywhere for a constant whose declared type is `secret`. The `mixed` result cannot be `secret`, so the value would lose that protection.; `LogicError` — The class declares and inherits no constant of that name. Or the constant's value is not a `string`, `int`, `bool` or `float` written directly in the code. `hasValue` checks this before the call. Both are mistakes in the program, not permission problems. That is how they differ from the `RuntimeError` above.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-hasmethod"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->hasMethod`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->hasMethod(string $name): bool
```

Checks whether the described class declares or inherits a method named `$name`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The method's name, as the declaration writes it and as `methods` returns it. |

**Returns** `bool` — `true` for a method of the class at any visibility. `false` if the class has no method with that name. So when a call fails, you can tell a `private` method from a misspelled name.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-attributes"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->attributes`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->attributes(): array<Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo>
```

Returns every `#[...]` attribute written on the class's own declaration or on its own properties and methods.

**Returns** `array<Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo>` — One `Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo` for each place an attribute is written, in source order. The class declaration's attributes come first, then those of each property and method. A method's parameters come after that method. **Only the class's own** declarations are included. `constants` also includes the parent classes. An attribute belongs to the declaration it is written on, so a parent class's attributes are not listed. `Core\Attributes::get` reads an attribute by the *shape* of its payload. It is checked at compile time and costs nothing at run time. Use `attributes` for a class whose name is not in your source code.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-get"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->get`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->get(mixed $object, string $name): mixed
```

Reads the `$name` property of `$object`. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$object` | `mixed` | An instance of the described class. The description is of a class and does not contain an object, so you pass the object to read here. |
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The property's name without the `$`, as `properties` returns it. |

**Returns** `mixed` — The property's value. Its type is `mixed`, whatever type the property declares.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — `$object` is not an object, or `$name` is a property that is not `public`. Reflection has the same visibility rules as ordinary code. Ordinary code outside the class gets the same error for this read.; `LogicError` — `$object` is not an instance of the described class, or the class has no property called `$name`. Both are mistakes in the program, not facts about the value. That is how they differ from the `RuntimeError` above.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-set"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->set`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->set(mixed $object, string $name, mixed $value): void
```

Writes the `$name` property of `$object`, and then runs the `PropertyObserver`, as an ordinary write does. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$object` | `mixed` | An instance of the described class. You pass it here for the same reason as in `get`. |
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The property's name without the `$`, as `properties` returns it. |
| `$value` | `mixed` | The value to store. It is checked against the type that the object's class declares for the property, because that type is not known at compile time. |

**Returns** `void` — Nothing. A following `get` returns the stored value, and the observer is told about that value.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — `$object` is not an object, `$name` is a property that is not `public`, or `$value` does not have the type that the property declares. Ordinary code outside the class gets the same errors for the first two. A write through a `mixed` value gets the same error for the third.; `LogicError` — `$object` is not an instance of the described class, or the class has no property called `$name`. As in `get`, these are mistakes in the program, so they have a different error class.; `Throwable` — Whatever the class's own `onPropertySet` observer throws. The observer runs after the value is stored. If it throws, the write still fails, as an ordinary write does.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-call"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->call`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->call(mixed $object, string $name, array<mixed> $arguments): mixed
```

Calls the `$name` method of `$object` with `$arguments`. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$object` | `mixed` | An instance of the described class. The description is of a class and does not contain an object, so you pass the object to call here. |
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The method's name without the `()`, as the declaration writes it. |
| `$arguments` | `array<mixed>` | One entry for each declared parameter, in order. Keys are ignored. Entries after the last parameter are ignored. This argument is required even when the method has no parameters. In that case, pass `[]`. |

**Returns** `mixed` — Whatever the method returned. Its type is `mixed`, whatever type the method declares.

**Throws** `LogicError` — `$name` is not `public`, is not a method of the class, or is a `Core` method. Or `$arguments` has fewer entries than the method's parameters, or an entry has a type that its parameter does not accept. An ordinary call on a `mixed` value throws the same error, from the same check.; `RuntimeError` — `$object` is not an object at all. A `$object` that is an object but not an instance of the described class is the `LogicError` above.

<a id="core-core-reflect-classinfo-construct"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo->construct`

```nvs skip
$classInfo->construct(array<mixed> $arguments): mixed
```

Builds an instance of the described class and runs its constructor with `$arguments`. The visibility rules are the same as for a `new` written at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$arguments` | `array<mixed>` | One entry for each declared constructor parameter, in order. Keys are ignored. Entries after the last parameter are ignored. This argument is required even when the class declares no constructor. In that case, pass `[]`. |

**Returns** `mixed` — The new instance. Its type is `mixed`. For a class with no constructor, the new instance has the default values that the class declares for its properties.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The constructor is not `public` and this call site is outside the class. Or `$arguments` has fewer entries than the constructor's parameters, or an entry has a type that its parameter does not accept. Or this program does not declare the described class. An ordinary `new` makes the same checks.

<a id="core-core-reflect-methodinfo-parameters"></a>

<a id="core-core-reflect-constantinfo-name"></a>

```nvs skip

```

The constant's name, as the declaring class writes it.

<a id="core-core-reflect-constantinfo-ispublic"></a>

```nvs skip
$constantInfo->isPublic(): bool
```

Checks whether code outside the declaring class may use the constant.

<a id="core-core-reflect-constantinfo-hasvalue"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo->hasValue`

```nvs skip
$constantInfo->hasValue(): bool
```

Checks whether Novis computes the constant's value at compile time. Only then can `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant` return it.

**Returns** `bool` — `true` for a `string`, `int`, `bool` or `float` written directly in the code. `false` for an `array` or object constant, and for an integer too large for `int`. Novis reads a constant only when its value is written directly in the code, and it does not evaluate other expressions. So this is `false` for exactly the constants that are also not allowed in type position.

<a id="core-core-reflect-attributeinfo"></a>
### `Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo`

Keywords: name, target, parameter, fields, field

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|

| [`Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo->parameter`](#core-core-reflect-attributeinfo-parameter) | `parameter(): string` |

<a id="core-core-reflect-attributeinfo-name"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo->name`

```nvs skip
$attributeInfo->name(): string
```

Returns the name of the `type` alias written in the attribute, as it is written.

**Returns** `string` — The written name. For the form `#[{...}]`, which has no name, it is the **empty string**. The name is not resolved. The compiler uses it to check the payload object where the attribute is written. Your code never uses it to find an attribute.

<a id="core-core-reflect-attributeinfo-target"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo->target`

```nvs skip
$attributeInfo->target(): string
```

Returns the property or method that the attribute is written on.

**Returns** `string` — A property's name without the `$`, or a method's name. For the class or interface declaration itself, it is the **empty string**. For an attribute on a parameter, this is the method's name, and `parameter` returns the parameter's name.

<a id="core-core-reflect-attributeinfo-parameter"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo->parameter`

```nvs skip
$attributeInfo->parameter(): string
```

The parameter of `target` the attribute is written on.

**Returns** `string` — The parameter's name without the `$`. For an attribute that is not on a parameter, it is the **empty string**. With `target`, you can tell `#[X] public function f(...)` from `public function f(#[X] int $n)`. These two attributes are on different declarations.

<a id="core-core-reflect-attributeinfo-fields"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo->fields`

```nvs skip
$attributeInfo->fields(): array<string>
```

The payload's field names, in the order the attribute writes them.

**Returns** `array<string>` — One string for each field. This includes a field whose value Novis does not compute here. `field` throws an error for such a field.

<a id="core-core-reflect-attributeinfo-field"></a>
#### `Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo->field`

```nvs skip
$attributeInfo->field(string $name): mixed
```

Returns one payload field's value, computed at compile time.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$name` | `string` (neutral) | The field's name, as `fields` returns it. |

**Returns** `mixed` — The value as a `string`, `int`, `bool` or `float`. These are the four types a payload field can have here.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The attribute's payload has no field of that name. This is a mistake in the program, so the method throws an error and does not return an empty value. `fields` returns the names that exist. Or Novis does not compute the field's value here. That is a class constant, an enum case or `Foo::class`, which depend on the namespace the attribute is *written* in. It is also any value that `Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo` cannot read. `Core\Attributes::get` reads all of these values at compile time, by shape.
