<a id="core-core-ldap-dn-of"></a>
#### `Core\Ldap\Dn::of`

```nvs skip
Core\Ldap\Dn::of(string $attribute, string $value): Core\Ldap\Dn
```

Returns a DN with one part, `attribute=value`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$attribute` | `string` (sink) | The attribute's name, such as `CN` or `OU`. It cannot be `tainted`. |
| `$value` | `string` (launder) | The value, such as `Ann Lee`. It can be `tainted`. A `,`, `+`, `=` or other special character in it is escaped, so it stays one value. |

**Returns** `Core\Ldap\Dn` — A `Core\Ldap\Dn`.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The attribute is not an attribute name, or the value is empty.

<a id="core-core-ldap-dn-child"></a>
#### `Core\Ldap\Dn->child`

```nvs skip
$dn->child(string $attribute, string $value): Core\Ldap\Dn
```

Returns the DN of an entry directly below this one. `attribute=value` is added at the start.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$attribute` | `string` (sink) | The attribute's name, such as `CN` or `OU`. It cannot be `tainted`. |
| `$value` | `string` (launder) | The value, such as `Ann Lee`. It can be `tainted`. A `,`, `+`, `=` or other special character in it is escaped, so it stays one value. |

**Returns** `Core\Ldap\Dn` — A new `Core\Ldap\Dn`. This DN does not change.

**Throws** `LogicError` — The attribute is not an attribute name, or the value is empty.

<a id="core-core-ldap-dn-parent"></a>
#### `Core\Ldap\Dn->parent`

```nvs skip
$dn->parent(): ?Core\Ldap\Dn
```

Returns the DN one level up. The first part is removed.

**Returns** `?Core\Ldap\Dn` — The parent DN, or `null` when this DN has only one part.

<a id="core-core-ldap-dn-rdnattribute"></a>
#### `Core\Ldap\Dn->rdnAttribute`

```nvs skip
$dn->rdnAttribute(): string
```

Returns the attribute name of the first part. For `CN=Ann Lee,OU=Staff,DC=example,DC=test` this is `CN`.

**Returns** `string` — The name, written as in the DN. When the first part has several values joined by `+`, it is the name of the first one.

<a id="core-core-ldap-dn-rdnvalue"></a>
#### `Core\Ldap\Dn->rdnValue`

```nvs skip
$dn->rdnValue(): tainted string
```

Returns the value of the first part, with escapes removed. For `CN=Lee\, Ann,OU=Staff,DC=example,DC=test` this is `Lee, Ann`.

**Returns** `tainted string` — The value. It is `tainted`. When the first part has several values joined by `+`, it is the first one.

<a id="core-core-ldap-dn-iswithin"></a>
#### `Core\Ldap\Dn->isWithin`

```nvs skip
$dn->isWithin(Core\Ldap\Dn $other): bool
```

Checks if this DN is `other` or an entry below it. Upper and lower case do not matter when names and values are compared.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$other` | `Core\Ldap\Dn` | The DN to compare with, such as `Dn::parse('DC=example,DC=test')`. |

**Returns** `bool` — `true` when this DN ends with every part of `other`.

<a id="core-core-ldap-dn-tostring"></a>
#### `Core\Ldap\Dn->toString`

```nvs skip
$dn->toString(): tainted string
```

Returns the DN as text, with each special character in a value escaped.

**Returns** `tainted string` — The text. `Dn::parse` reads it back as the same DN. The text is `tainted`, because a value in the DN may be.


<a id="core-core-queue"></a>
### `Core\Queue`

Keywords: push, status, cancel, stats, delete, purge

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Core\Queue::push`](#core-core-queue-push) | `push(string $script, { args?: mixed, queue?: string, runAt?: Core\Time\Instant, maxAttempts?: uint, backoff?: Core\Time\Duration, key?: string, tag?: string, grants?: array<string>, memory?: string, cpuTime?: string, wallTime?: string, maxOutput?: string }): Core\Queue\Id` |
| [`Core\Queue::status`](#core-core-queue-status) | `status(Core\Queue\Id $job): Core\Queue::State` |
| [`Core\Queue::cancel`](#core-core-queue-cancel) | `cancel(Core\Queue\Id $job): bool` |
| [`Core\Queue::stats`](#core-core-queue-stats) | `stats(string $queue): Core\Queue\Stats` |
| [`Core\Queue::delete`](#core-core-queue-delete) | `delete(Core\Queue\Id $job): bool` |
| [`Core\Queue::purge`](#core-core-queue-purge) | `purge(string $queue, { state?: Core\Queue::State, tag?: string, before?: Core\Time\Instant, limit?: uint }): uint` |

<a id="core-core-queue-push"></a>
#### `Core\Queue::push`

```nvs skip
Core\Queue::push(string $script, { args?: mixed, queue?: string, runAt?: Core\Time\Instant, maxAttempts?: uint, backoff?: Core\Time\Duration, key?: string, tag?: string, grants?: array<string>, memory?: string, cpuTime?: string, wallTime?: string, maxOutput?: string }): Core\Queue\Id
```

Adds a job that runs `$script` in the background. The job is a row in the database set by `[queue] connection`. Inside a transaction on that connection, the job is saved only when the transaction commits. If the transaction rolls back, the job is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$script` | `string` (sink) | The path of the file a worker runs, written the way `spawn script` writes one. A relative path starts at the folder of the file that calls `push`. It is a file, not a class or a function, so the job has no captured variables. |
| `{ args: … }` | `mixed` (default `(omitted)`) | The data the job receives. It is copied into the row and decoded into the types the job declares. It is never passed by reference, because the worker usually runs in another process. |
| `{ queue: … }` | `string` (default `"default"`, neutral) | The name of the queue the job goes in. Each worker takes jobs from the queues it is configured for, so you can keep slow work and fast work apart. |
| `{ runAt: … }` | `Core\Time\Instant` (default `null`) | The earliest time a worker may start the job. The default is now. |
| `{ maxAttempts: … }` | `uint` (default `null`) | How many times the job may run before it moves to the dead-letter table (the table of jobs that failed too often). The default is `[queue] max_attempts`. The number is always finite, so a job cannot retry forever. |
| `{ backoff: … }` | `Core\Time\Duration` (default `null`) | The base wait between two attempts. The wait grows after each failed attempt, and the worker adds a small random amount. The default is one second. |
| `{ key: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | A key that stops duplicate jobs. While a job with this key is still pending, a second `push` with the same key adds nothing. It returns the id of the pending job. |
| `{ tag: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | A group name for the job. Many jobs can have the same tag. Only `purge` reads it, to delete one group of jobs. You cannot add a tag after the `push`. |
| `{ grants: … }` | `array<string>` (default `null`) | The capabilities the job may use, written the way `nvs.toml` grants them. The list may only contain capabilities this request has. The default is what this request has. `[]` gives the job no capabilities. |
| `{ memory: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The memory limit for the job, written like `[limits] memory`. `[limits.hard]` sets the highest value allowed. The default is the limit of this request. |
| `{ cpuTime: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The CPU time limit for the job, written like `[limits] cpu_time`. It follows the same rules as `memory`. |
| `{ wallTime: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The real time limit for the job, written like `[limits] wall_time`. It follows the same rules as `memory`. |
| `{ maxOutput: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | The limit on the output the job may print, written like `[limits] max_output`. It follows the same rules as `memory`. |

**Returns** `Core\Queue\Id` — A `Core\Queue\Id` for the new job. You pass it to `status`, `cancel` and `delete`. When `key` finds a pending job, it is the id of that job.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration has no `[queue]` block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet. It is also thrown when `grants` contains a capability this request does not have.; `LogicError` — `maxAttempts` is `0`, or `backoff` is negative. It is also thrown when `grants` contains a name that is not a capability, or a limit is one this request may not set.; `IOError` — The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the insert. The most common cause is that `nvs queue migrate` has not created the table yet.

<a id="core-core-queue-status"></a>
#### `Core\Queue::status`

```nvs skip
Core\Queue::status(Core\Queue\Id $job): Core\Queue::State
```

Returns the current state of one job, as a `Core\Queue::State` case. Every call reads the state from the database.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$job` | `Core\Queue\Id` | The `Core\Queue\Id` that `push` returned. It identifies the job and its queue. |

**Returns** `Core\Queue::State` — `Pending` while the job waits, also while its `runAt` time or its backoff has not passed. `Claimed` while a worker runs it, `Succeeded` after it ran, `Dead` after it used all its attempts, and `Cancelled` after `cancel` stopped it.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration has no `[queue]` block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet. It is also thrown when neither table has the job, for example because `delete` deleted it.; `IOError` — The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the query. The most common cause is that `nvs queue migrate` has not created the tables yet.

<a id="core-core-queue-cancel"></a>
#### `Core\Queue::cancel`

```nvs skip
Core\Queue::cancel(Core\Queue\Id $job): bool
```

Removes one job from the queue if it is still waiting. A job that a worker already started keeps running, because `cancel` does not stop work in progress.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$job` | `Core\Queue\Id` | The `Core\Queue\Id` that `push` returned. It identifies the job and its queue. |

**Returns** `bool` — `true` if this call cancelled the job. `false` if the job was no longer waiting: a worker took it, it already ran, or an earlier `cancel` removed it. After `true`, `status` returns `Cancelled`.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration has no `[queue]` block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet.; `IOError` — The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the update. The most common cause is that `nvs queue migrate` has not created the table yet.

<a id="core-core-queue-stats"></a>
#### `Core\Queue::stats`

```nvs skip
Core\Queue::stats(string $queue): Core\Queue\Stats
```

Counts the jobs of one queue. The result has five numbers: waiting jobs, running jobs, attempts used, jobs in the dead-letter table, and the attempts those jobs used. All five are read at the same moment.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$queue` | `string` (neutral) | The name of the queue, the same name `push` used in its `queue` option. Each call counts one queue. |

**Returns** `Core\Queue\Stats` — A `Core\Queue\Stats`. Each number is a method, so you write `$stats->pending()`, not `$stats->pending`.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration has no `[queue]` block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet.; `IOError` — The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the query. The most common cause is that `nvs queue migrate` has not created the tables yet.

<a id="core-core-queue-delete"></a>
#### `Core\Queue::delete`

```nvs skip
Core\Queue::delete(Core\Queue\Id $job): bool
```

Deletes the row of one job. The row can be in the jobs table or in the dead-letter table. A job that a worker is running is not deleted. You need the `queue.purge` capability for the queue of the job.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$job` | `Core\Queue\Id` | The `Core\Queue\Id` that `push` returned. It still works after the job moves to the dead-letter table. |

**Returns** `bool` — `true` if this call deleted the row. `false` if there was nothing to delete: a worker is running the job, the job is not in this queue, or an earlier `delete` deleted it. After `true`, the row is gone, so `status` throws an error for this job.

**Throws** `RuntimeError` — The configuration grants no `queue.purge` for the queue of the job. A server has no such grant until the person who runs it adds one. It is also thrown when there is no `[queue]` block, or the database driver cannot run statements yet.; `IOError` — The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the delete. The most common cause is that `nvs queue migrate` has not created the tables yet.

<a id="core-core-queue-purge"></a>
#### `Core\Queue::purge`

```nvs skip
Core\Queue::purge(string $queue, { state?: Core\Queue::State, tag?: string, before?: Core\Time\Instant, limit?: uint }): uint
```

Deletes the finished jobs of a queue and returns how many rows it deleted. Without `state`, it deletes the `Succeeded` and `Cancelled` jobs. `Dead` and `Pending` jobs are deleted only when you pass that state. `Claimed` jobs are never deleted. One call deletes at most `limit` rows, so you call it again until it returns `0`. You need the `queue.purge` capability for the queue.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$queue` | `string` (neutral) | The name of the queue. It must match the name `push` used exactly. The `queue.purge` capability is checked for this name. |
| `{ state: … }` | `Core\Queue::State` (default `null`) | One `Core\Queue::State` to delete in place of the default ones. `Dead` deletes from the dead-letter table. `Pending` deletes jobs that have not run yet. `Claimed` throws an error, because a worker is running those jobs. |
| `{ tag: … }` | `string` (default `null`, neutral) | Deletes only the jobs that `push` gave this tag. |
| `{ before: … }` | `Core\Time\Instant` (default `null`) | Deletes only the jobs added before this time. This is the time of the `push`, not the time of the next attempt. |
| `{ limit: … }` | `uint` (default `1000`) | The most rows one call deletes, oldest first. The default is `1000`. A delete without a limit can lock the table for a long time, and every `push` waits for it. |

**Returns** `uint` — The number of rows this call deleted, and `0` when nothing matched. `while (Core\Queue::purge('email') > 0) {}` deletes all of them, one batch at a time.

**Throws** `LogicError` — `state` is `Core\Queue::State::Claimed`. A worker is running those jobs, so their rows cannot be deleted.; `RuntimeError` — The configuration grants no `queue.purge` for this queue. A server has no such grant until the person who runs it adds one. It is also thrown when there is no `[queue]` block, or the database driver cannot run statements yet.; `IOError` — The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the delete. The most common cause is that `nvs queue migrate` has not created the tables yet.

| [`Core\Queue\Stats->deadAttempts`](#core-core-queue-stats-deadattempts) | `deadAttempts(): uint` |
| [`Core\Queue\Stats->nonTransactional`](#core-core-queue-stats-nontransactional) | `nonTransactional(): uint` |

<a id="core-core-queue-stats-pending"></a>
#### `Core\Queue\Stats->pending`

```nvs skip
$stats->pending(): uint
```

The number of jobs that wait for a worker. This includes jobs whose `runAt` time is still in the future, and jobs that wait between two attempts.

**Returns** `uint` — A `uint`. It is `0` for a new queue and for a queue with no work left.

<a id="core-core-queue-stats-claimed"></a>
#### `Core\Queue\Stats->claimed`

```nvs skip
$stats->claimed(): uint
```

The number of jobs that a worker is running now. A job whose worker stopped is still counted here. After the `[queue] visibility` time, another worker can start it again.

**Returns** `uint` — A `uint`. When it equals the number of jobs your workers can run at once, the queue is busy but not stuck.

<a id="core-core-queue-stats-attempts"></a>
#### `Core\Queue\Stats->attempts`

```nvs skip
$stats->attempts(): uint
```

The total number of attempts the jobs of this queue have used. If this number grows and `pending` does not, jobs are failing and running again.

**Returns** `uint` — A `uint` for the jobs table only. The jobs in the dead-letter table are counted by `deadLettered` and `deadAttempts`.

<a id="core-core-queue-stats-deadlettered"></a>
#### `Core\Queue\Stats->deadLettered`

```nvs skip
$stats->deadLettered(): uint
```

The number of jobs that used all their attempts and are now in the dead-letter table. These jobs did not finish, so this is a good number to alert on.

**Returns** `uint` — A `uint`. It goes down only when `purge` or `delete` deletes a job from the dead-letter table.

<a id="core-core-queue-stats-deadattempts"></a>
#### `Core\Queue\Stats->deadAttempts`

```nvs skip
$stats->deadAttempts(): uint
```

The total number of attempts the jobs in the dead-letter table used. Divide it by `deadLettered` to see how many attempts a job uses before it fails for good.

**Returns** `uint` — A `uint` for the dead-letter table only. Every attempt is counted in this number or in `attempts`, never in both. Add the two to get the total.

<a id="core-core-queue-stats-nontransactional"></a>
#### `Core\Queue\Stats->nonTransactional`

```nvs skip
$stats->nonTransactional(): uint
```

The number of jobs that `push` saved while a transaction was open on a different database connection. Such a job is saved at once, so a rollback of that transaction does not remove it.

**Returns** `uint` — A `uint` for the jobs table only. It is `0` when every transaction that pushes a job runs on the connection that `[queue] connection` names.

<a id="core-novis-image-image"></a>
### `Novis\Image\Image`

Keywords: image, picture, thumbnail, resize, scale, crop, rotate, convert, image size, image dimensions, jpeg, png, webp, open, create, fromRaw, info, mime, extension, resize, crop, trim, rotate, flip, composite, flatten, sharpen, blur, grayscale, brightness, contrast, gamma, tint, text, measureText, format, metadata, encode, raw, variants, compare, hash, hashDistance, placeholder, palette

`Novis\Image\Image` is an image and a list of steps to run on it. Each step method, such as
`resize`, `crop` or `format`, returns a new `Image` and does not change the old one. No pixel is
decoded until `encode`, `variants` or `raw` runs the steps, so bytes that are not an image throw a
`ParseError` only then. `encode` removes all metadata, such as the place a photo was taken, unless
`metadata({ keep: true })` is a step.

```nvs
<?nvs
use Novis\Image\Format;
use Novis\Image\Image;

// A PNG of 3 by 2 pixels, written as hex.
bytes $png = Core\Encoding::fromHex(
    '89504e470d0a1a0a0000000d49484452000000030000000208060000009d74661a'
        . '0000000b49444154789c6360c00500001a0001bc3ce0410000000049454e44ae426082',
);

Image $photo = Image::open($png);
bytes $thumb = $photo->resize({ width: 6, upscale: true })->format(Format::Jpeg, { quality: 80 })->encode();

var $info = Image::info($thumb);
echo Image::mime($info->format), ' ', $info->width, 'x', $info->height, "\n";
```
```output
image/jpeg 6x4
```

|---|---|

<a id="core-novis-image-image-open"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image::open`

```nvs skip
Novis\Image\Image::open(bytes $data, ?{ autoOrient?: bool, toSrgb?: bool, maxPixels?: uint, page?: uint, dpi?: float } $options = null): Image
```

`Image::open` starts from the bytes of an encoded image. It turns the image upright and
converts its colours to sRGB, unless `autoOrient` or `toSrgb` is `false`.
`page` chooses one page of a document, starting at 1. `dpi` is the resolution of that page, 150 by default.
An image with one page has only page 1, and a page past the end throws an error.
Bytes that are not an image throw an error when `encode`, `variants` or `raw` runs.

**Returns** `Image`

`Image::create` starts from a blank canvas. Without `$fill`, the canvas is transparent.

**Returns** `Image`

With both, `fit` decides how the image fills that size. The default is `Fit::Cover`.
The image does not grow larger than it is, unless `upscale` is `true`.

<a id="core-novis-image-image-flip"></a>

<a id="core-novis-image-image-composite"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image->composite`

```nvs skip
$image->composite(Image $overlay, ?{ gravity?: Gravity, x?: int, y?: int, opacity?: float, blend?: Blend } $options = null): Image
```

`composite` draws `$overlay` on top of this image, with all of the overlay's own steps.
`gravity` places it, and the default is `Gravity::Center`. `x` and `y` place its top-left
corner in pixels instead, and may be negative. The parts outside this image are cut off.
`opacity` is from 0.0 to 1.0, and the default is 1.0. `blend` mixes the colours, and the
default is `Blend::Normal`. A `format` or `metadata` step of the overlay changes nothing.

**Returns** `Image`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-text"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image->text`

```nvs skip
$image->text(string $text, Font $font, { size: float, color: Color, gravity?: Gravity, x?: int, y?: int, maxWidth?: uint, align?: Align } $options): Image
```

`text` draws `$text` on the image with `$font`, in `color`. `size` is the font size in pixels.
`x` and `y` place the top-left corner of the text. Without them, `gravity` places it, and
the default is `Gravity::Center`. With `maxWidth`, lines break at spaces to stay that wide.
`align` sets how the lines line up, and the default is `Align::Left`. Text in any script
is drawn as the font defines it. A line of Arabic or Hebrew runs from right to left.

**Returns** `Image`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-measuretext"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image::measureText`

```nvs skip
Novis\Image\Image::measureText(string $text, Font $font, { size: float, maxWidth?: uint, align?: Align } $options): Size
```

`Image::measureText` returns the `width` and `height` in pixels that `text` needs for the same text and options.

**Returns** `Size`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-format"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image->format`

```nvs skip
$image->format(Format $format, ?{ quality?: uint, progressive?: bool, lossless?: bool, effort?: uint } $options = null): Image
```

`format` sets the format that `encode` writes. Without it, the output has the format of the input.

**Returns** `Image`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-metadata"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image->metadata`

```nvs skip
$image->metadata({ keep: bool } $options): Image
```

`metadata({ keep: true })` keeps the EXIF data in the output. Without it, `encode` removes all metadata.

**Returns** `Image`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-encode"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image->encode`

```nvs skip
$image->encode(): bytes
```

`encode` runs every step and returns the encoded file.

<a id="core-novis-image-image-raw"></a>

```nvs skip
$image->raw(): Raw
```

`raw` runs every step and returns the pixels as RGBA8 rows, four bytes per pixel.

<a id="core-novis-image-image-variants"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image->variants`

```nvs skip
$image->variants(array<Variant> $set): array<bytes>
```

`variants` decodes the image once and returns one encoded file per entry, in the same order.
An entry may resize the image and choose its own format and quality.

**Returns** `array<bytes>`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-compare"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image::compare`

```nvs skip
Novis\Image\Image::compare(bytes|Image $a, bytes|Image $b, ?{ tolerance?: uint, render?: bool } $options = null): Diff
```

`Image::compare` compares two images of the same size and returns a `Diff`. Other sizes throw a `LogicError`.
A pixel differs when its delta is above `tolerance`, which is 0 by default.

**Returns** `Diff`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-hash"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image::hash`

```nvs skip
Novis\Image\Image::hash(bytes $data, HashKind $kind): bytes
```

`Image::hash` returns a short hash of an encoded image. Two similar images have similar hashes.
Each `HashKind` returns a hash of its own fixed length.

**Returns** `bytes`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-hashdistance"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image::hashDistance`

```nvs skip
Novis\Image\Image::hashDistance(bytes $a, bytes $b): uint
```

`Image::hashDistance` returns how many bits differ between two hashes. A small number means similar images.
Two hashes of different lengths throw a `LogicError`.

**Returns** `uint`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-placeholder"></a>

```nvs skip
Novis\Image\Image::placeholder(bytes $data, PlaceholderKind $kind): string
```

`Image::placeholder` returns a short text that a web page can draw as a blurred preview of the image.
Its average colour is the average colour of the image.

**Returns** `string`

<a id="core-novis-image-image-palette"></a>
#### `Novis\Image\Image::palette`

```nvs skip
Novis\Image\Image::palette(bytes $data, uint $count = 5): array<Color>
```

`Image::palette` returns at most `count` main colours of the image, the most common first.
Transparent pixels are not counted. A `count` above 256 throws a `LogicError`.

**Returns** `array<Color>`


`QrCode::giroCode` returns the text of a SEPA bank transfer, for a QR code that a banking app reads.

#### `Novis\Intl\Collator::sort`

```nvs skip
Novis\Intl\Collator::sort(array<string> $strings, string $locale, ?CollateOptions $options = null): array<string>
```

`Collator::sort` returns the strings sorted by the rules of `$locale`. Equal strings
keep their order. A locale tag that is not valid throws a `LogicError`.

**Returns** `array<string>`

<a id="core-novis-intl-collator-sortkeys"></a>
#### `Novis\Intl\Collator::sortKeys`

```nvs skip

```

`Collator::sortKeys` returns one sort key for each string. Keys compare byte by byte in the
order `sort` gives their strings. You can store a key in a column and sort rows by it.

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document"></a>
### `Novis\Pdf\Document`

Keywords: pdf, generate pdf, html to pdf, wkhtmltopdf, invoice, report, page number, header, footer, pdf/a, factur-x, fromHtml, asset, standard, invoiceXml, password, created, header, footer, slots, render

`Novis\Pdf\Document` is an HTML document that `render` turns into a PDF file. Each method returns a
new `Document` and does not change the old one. The render reads only the files you add with `asset`
and `data:` URIs, so a name that is not an asset throws a `LogicError`. `render` returns a
`Rendered` with the file, its page count, and the CSS it could not draw.

```nvs
<?nvs
use Novis\Pdf\Document;
use Novis\Pdf\Page;

// The logo is a file that the HTML names. `asset` adds it to the document.
bytes $logo = "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"40\" height=\"20\"><rect width=\"40\" height=\"20\"/></svg>" as bytes;
string $html = "<html lang=\"en\"><head><title>Invoice 1042</title></head><body>"
    . "<img src=\"logo.svg\" alt=\"Shop\"><h1>Invoice 1042</h1><p>Tea: 2.50 EUR</p></body></html>";

// The footer is a function. The render calls it once for each page.
var $rendered = Document::fromHtml($html)
    ->asset('logo.svg', $logo)
    ->footer(fn(Page $page): Core\Html\Markup => html`<p>Page {$page->number} of {$page->count}</p>`)
    ->render();

echo Core\Bytes::startsWith($rendered->bytes, '%PDF-' as bytes) ? 'a PDF file' : 'not a PDF file', "\n";
echo $rendered->pageCount, " page\n";
```
```output
a PDF file
1 page
```

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document::fromHtml`](#core-novis-pdf-document-fromhtml) | `fromHtml(Core\Html\Markup\|string $html): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->asset`](#core-novis-pdf-document-asset) | `asset(string $name, bytes $data): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->standard`](#core-novis-pdf-document-standard) | `standard(Standard $standard): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->invoiceXml`](#core-novis-pdf-document-invoicexml) | `invoiceXml(string $xml): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->password`](#core-novis-pdf-document-password) | `password(string $password): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->created`](#core-novis-pdf-document-created) | `created(Core\Time\Instant $at): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->header`](#core-novis-pdf-document-header) | `header(callable(Page): Core\Html\Markup $fn, ?{ height?: string } $options = null): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->footer`](#core-novis-pdf-document-footer) | `footer(callable(Page): Core\Html\Markup $fn, ?{ height?: string } $options = null): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->slots`](#core-novis-pdf-document-slots) | `slots(callable(Page): array<Core\Html\Markup> $fn): Document` |
| [`Novis\Pdf\Document->render`](#core-novis-pdf-document-render) | `render(): Rendered` |

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-fromhtml"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document::fromHtml`

```nvs skip
Novis\Pdf\Document::fromHtml(Core\Html\Markup|string $html): Document
```

`Document::fromHtml` starts a document from its HTML.
The HTML may name assets, such as `<img src="logo.png">`. Add each one with `asset`.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-asset"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->asset`

```nvs skip
$document->asset(string $name, bytes $data): Document
```

`asset` adds a file the HTML names, such as an image or a stylesheet.
A render reads only these files and `data:` URIs. Any other name throws a `LogicError`.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-standard"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->standard`

```nvs skip
$document->standard(Standard $standard): Document
```

`standard` sets the PDF standard the file follows.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-invoicexml"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->invoiceXml`

```nvs skip
$document->invoiceXml(string $xml): Document
```

`invoiceXml` attaches the XML of an electronic invoice to the file.
It needs the standard `Document::Standard::PdfA3b`. With any other standard, `render` throws a `LogicError`.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-password"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->password`

```nvs skip
$document->password(string $password): Document
```

`password` encrypts the file. A reader needs the password to open it.
A PDF/A standard does not allow a password, so `render` then throws a `LogicError`.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-created"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->created`

```nvs skip
$document->created(Core\Time\Instant $at): Document
```

`created` sets the creation time in the file. Without it, the file has no creation time.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-header"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->header`

```nvs skip
$document->header(callable(Page): Core\Html\Markup $fn, ?{ height?: string } $options = null): Document
```

`header` sets a function that returns the header of each page. `render` calls it once for each page.
The header is drawn in the top margin. `height` sets that margin, such as `"2cm"`. Without it, the margin is the one `@page` gives.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-footer"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->footer`

```nvs skip
$document->footer(callable(Page): Core\Html\Markup $fn, ?{ height?: string } $options = null): Document
```

`footer` sets a function that returns the footer of each page. It works like `header`, in the bottom margin.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-slots"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->slots`

```nvs skip
$document->slots(callable(Page): array<Core\Html\Markup> $fn): Document
```

`slots` sets a function that fills each `<slot name="...">` in a table row. `render` calls it once for each page.
It returns the HTML for each slot name. Nothing on the page moves, and HTML too tall for its cell is listed in `Rendered::overflows`.

**Returns** `Document`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-document-render"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Document->render`

```nvs skip
$document->render(): Rendered
```

`render` returns the PDF file and its pages.
Two renders of the same document give the same bytes.

**Returns** `Rendered`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-pages"></a>
### `Novis\Pdf\Pages`

Keywords: of, merge

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|

| [`Novis\Pdf\Pages::merge`](#core-novis-pdf-pages-merge) | `merge(array<Pages> $parts): bytes` |

<a id="core-novis-pdf-pages-of"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Pages::of`

```nvs skip
Novis\Pdf\Pages::of(bytes $pdf, ?array<uint> $pages = null): Pages
```

`Pages::of` chooses pages of a PDF file, in the order of `$pages`. Pages count from 1.
Without `$pages`, every page is chosen. A page listed twice is used twice, and a page not listed is left out.

**Returns** `Pages`

<a id="core-novis-pdf-pages-merge"></a>
#### `Novis\Pdf\Pages::merge`

```nvs skip
Novis\Pdf\Pages::merge(array<Pages> $parts): bytes
```

`Pages::merge` returns one PDF file with the chosen pages of each part, in order.
A page number past the end of its file throws a `LogicError`. A file that is encrypted or does not parse throws a `ParseError`.

**Returns** `bytes`

### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Formula`

Keywords: constructor, of

| Member | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`Novis\Spreadsheet\Formula::constructor`](#core-novis-spreadsheet-formula-constructor) | `constructor(tainted string $text, string\|int\|float\|null $cached)` |

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-formula-constructor"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Formula::constructor`

```nvs skip
new Novis\Spreadsheet\Formula(tainted string $text, string|int|float|null $cached)
```

`new Formula` makes a formula from its values. `Formula::of` makes one for you.
`text` has no `=` at the start. It is `tainted`, because `Reader` can read a formula from a file. `cached` is the result the file has for a program that does not calculate.

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-formula-of"></a>

```nvs skip
Novis\Spreadsheet\Formula::of(string $text, ?{ cached?: string|int|float } $options = null): Formula
```

`Formula::of` makes a formula from its Excel text, such as `'SUM(C2:C9)'`. You can write the text with or without `=` at the start.
`cached` is the result the file has for a program that does not calculate. Excel calculates every formula again when it opens the file.

**Returns** `Formula`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-open"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader::open`

```nvs skip
Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader::open(tainted bytes|Core\IO\File $source): Reader
```

`Reader::open` opens the workbook in `$source`, the bytes of the file or a file your program opened. Another file type throws an error.
An xls or ods file is read whole here. A CSV file is UTF-8 text with one sheet, `Sheet1`, and each value in it is a `string`.

**Returns** `Reader`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-sheets"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->sheets`

```nvs skip
$reader->sheets(): array<SheetInfo>
```

`sheets` returns each sheet in tab order, with its name, its position from 0, whether it is hidden, its size and its kind.

**Returns** `array<SheetInfo>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-macros"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->macros`

```nvs skip
$reader->macros(): array<tainted string>
```

`macros` returns the names of the macro modules in an xlsm or xls file. The list is empty when the file has no macros.
Reading a file never runs its macros.

**Returns** `array<tainted string>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-merged"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->merged`

```nvs skip
$reader->merged(string|int $sheet): array<tainted string>
```

`merged` returns the merged cells of the sheet `$sheet`, by name or by position from 0. Each one is a range such as `"A1:C2"`.
When you read rows, the value of a merged range is in its top-left cell. With `merged: 'fill'`, every cell of the range has that value.

**Returns** `array<tainted string>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-links"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->links`

```nvs skip
$reader->links(string|int $sheet): array<Link>
```

`links` returns the hyperlinks of the sheet `$sheet`. `anchor` is the cell, such as `"B2"`, and `target` is where the link goes.
`external` is `true` for a URL or a file. Reading a file never opens its links.

**Returns** `array<Link>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-notes"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->notes`

```nvs skip
$reader->notes(string|int $sheet): array<Note>
```

`notes` returns the notes of the sheet `$sheet`. Each one has its cell in `noted`, its text in `note`, and its `author`.

**Returns** `array<Note>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-names"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->names`

```nvs skip
$reader->names(): array<Name>
```

`names` returns the defined names of the workbook. `reference` is the text of the name, such as `"Shop!$A$1:$C$9"`.
`sheet` is `null` for a name the whole workbook can use.

**Returns** `array<Name>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-tables"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->tables`

```nvs skip
$reader->tables(string|int $sheet): array<Table>
```

`tables` returns the Excel tables of the sheet `$sheet`. `table` is the range, such as `"A1:C10"`, and `name` is the table name.

**Returns** `array<Table>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-images"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->images`

```nvs skip
$reader->images(string|int $sheet): array<Image>
```

`images` returns the pictures of the sheet `$sheet`. `at` is the top-left cell, and `image` is the bytes of the picture.
A linked picture has empty `image` bytes, and `link` is its target. Reading a file never fetches a link.

**Returns** `array<Image>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-properties"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->properties`

```nvs skip
$reader->properties(): Properties
```

`properties` returns the title, subject, author, company and keywords of the workbook, and the time it was created.
A property the file does not have is `null`, and every property of a CSV file is `null`. An xls or ods file throws an error.

**Returns** `Properties`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-reader-rows"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Reader->rows`

```nvs skip
$reader->rows(string|int $sheet, RowOptions $options = null): Iterator<Row>
```

`rows` reads the sheet `$sheet`, by name or by position from 0, and gives one `Row` at a time. With `header: true`, the keys are the header cells.
`text: ["Zip"]` reads the column `Zip` as the text Excel shows, so `1234` with the format `00000` is `"01234"`. `text: true` reads every column this way.

**Returns** `Iterator<Row>`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-add"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->add`

```nvs skip
$sheet->add(array<mixed> $row, RowOptions $options = null): Sheet
```

`add` adds one row to the end of the sheet. A value goes to the column of its key, or by position from column `A`.
`height` is the row height in points. `hidden` hides the row. `level` puts it in an outline group. `style` is its `Style`.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-addall"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->addAll`

```nvs skip
$sheet->addAll(array<array<mixed>>|Iterable<array<mixed>>|Iterator<array<mixed>> $rows): Sheet
```

`addAll` adds each row of `$rows` in order, as `add` does.
`$rows` can be an array or a generator, so a long list of rows does not have to be in memory.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-cell"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->cell`

```nvs skip
$sheet->cell(string $key, int $row): string
```

`cell` returns the address of the column `$key` in row `$row`, such as `'C7'`.
`$key` is a column key or a column letter, such as `'qty'` or `'C'`.

**Returns** `string`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-column"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->column`

```nvs skip
$sheet->column(string $key): string
```

`column` returns the cells of the column `$key` in the rows added so far, such as `'C2:C1043'`.
The header row is not in the range. Call it after the last row to get every row.

**Returns** `string`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-merge"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->merge`

```nvs skip
$sheet->merge(string $range): Sheet
```

`merge` joins the cells of `$range`, such as `'A1:C1'`, into one cell.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-link"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->link`

```nvs skip
$sheet->link(string $cell, string $target, ?{ text?: string, tooltip?: string } $options = null): Sheet
```

`link` makes the cell `$cell` a link to `$target`. The target is an `http:` or `https:` address, a `mailto:` address, or a cell such as `'Totals!A1'`.
`text` is the text the cell shows. `tooltip` is the text a person sees over the link.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-note"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->note`

```nvs skip
$sheet->note(string $cell, string $text, ?{ author?: string } $options = null): Sheet
```

`note` adds the note `$text` to the cell `$cell`. `author` is the name the note shows.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-validate"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->validate`

```nvs skip
$sheet->validate(string $range, Validation $rule): Sheet
```

`validate` checks what a person types into `$range` in Excel. Give one of `list`, `whole`, `decimal`, `date`, `length` or `formula`.
`min` and `max` are the limits of a number, a date or a length. `input` is a message Excel shows, and `error` the message for a wrong value.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-group"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->group`

```nvs skip
$sheet->group(string $rows, ?{ collapsed?: bool } $options = null): Sheet
```

`group` puts the rows `$rows`, such as `'5:9'`, or the columns, such as `'B:D'`, in an outline group.
Add a group of rows before its rows, and a group of columns before the first row. `collapsed` hides the group.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-table"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->table`

```nvs skip
$sheet->table(string $range, TableOptions $options = null): Sheet
```

`table` makes the cells of `$range`, such as `'A1:C9'`, an Excel table. Its first row is the header row.
`totals` adds a row after the table. It maps a header to `'sum'`, `'average'`, `'count'`, `'min'`, `'max'` or a `Formula`.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-conditional"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->conditional`

```nvs skip
$sheet->conditional(string $range, Conditional $rule): Sheet
```

`conditional` adds one conditional format to `$range`. `kind` is `'cell'`, `'formula'`, `'colorScale'`, `'dataBar'`, `'iconSet'`, `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'duplicates'` or `'unique'`.
`values` are Excel formula text, so a text value has quotes, such as `'"open"'`. `style` is the `Style` of the cells the rule matches.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-image"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->image`

```nvs skip
$sheet->image(string $cell, bytes $data, ?{ width?: float, height?: float, offsetX?: float, offsetY?: float } $options = null): Sheet
```

`image` puts the PNG, JPEG or GIF image `$data` at the cell `$cell`. Any other format throws a `LogicError`.
`width` and `height` are in pixels. `offsetX` and `offsetY` move the image from the corner of the cell.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-chart"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->chart`

```nvs skip
$sheet->chart(string $cell, Chart $chart, ?{ width?: float, height?: float } $options = null): Sheet
```

`chart` puts `$chart` at the cell `$cell`. `width` and `height` are in pixels. The chart is 480 by 288 pixels if you do not set them.
A series range from `column` grows with the sheet, so a chart you add before the last row still shows every row.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-print"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->print`

```nvs skip
$sheet->print(PrintOptions $options): Sheet
```

`print` sets how the sheet is printed. `orientation` is `'portrait'` or `'landscape'`. `fitToPage` sets the number of pages wide and tall.
`repeatRows`, such as `'1:1'`, prints those rows on every page. `area` is the range to print. Set `fitToPage` before the first row.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-sheet-protect"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet->protect`

```nvs skip
$sheet->protect(?{ password?: string, allow?: array<string> } $options = null): Sheet
```

`protect` locks the layout of the sheet, so a person cannot change it in Excel. It is not a security feature: any tool can remove the password.
`allow` names what a person can still do, such as `'sort'` or `'autoFilter'`.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-template"></a>
### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Template`

Keywords: open, set, fill

| Member | Signature |

| [`Novis\Spreadsheet\Template->fill`](#core-novis-spreadsheet-template-fill) | `fill(array<mixed> $data): Export` |

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-template-open"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Template::open`

```nvs skip
Novis\Spreadsheet\Template::open(bytes|Core\IO\File $source, Options $options = null): Template
```

`Template::open` opens the template in `$source`, the bytes of an xlsx or xlsm file or a file your program opened.
The filled file copies the formulas, links and sheets of the template without any change. For this reason, `$source` cannot be `tainted`, such as an uploaded file.
To fill an uploaded template, call `Core\Taint::assertTrusted` on its bytes first, with the reason you trust it.
`zone` is the time zone for an `Instant`, such as `'Europe/Berlin'`. Without `zone`, an `Instant` throws an error.

**Returns** `Template`

#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Template->set`

```nvs skip
$template->set(string $address, mixed $value): Template
```

`set` puts `$value` in the cell at `$address`, such as `'Summary!B2'`. Call it before `fill`.

**Returns** `Template`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-template-fill"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Template->fill`

```nvs skip
$template->fill(array<mixed> $data): Export
```

`fill` puts the value at each placeholder's path in `$data` into its cell. A placeholder that `$data` does not have throws an error.
The file is written when you call `download`, `save`, `to` or `bytes` on the result.

**Returns** `Export`

The path needs the `fs.write` capability in `nvs.toml`.

```nvs skip
Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook::createForStream(Core\IO\File $file, Options $options = null): Workbook
```

`Workbook::createForStream` writes the file to `$file`, a file that your program opened for writing.
`finish` does not close `$file`.

**Returns** `Workbook`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-workbook-createinmemory"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook::createInMemory`

```nvs skip
Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook::createInMemory(Options $options = null): Workbook
```

**Returns** `Workbook`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-workbook-fromrows"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook::fromRows`

```nvs skip
Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook::fromRows(array<array<mixed>>|Iterable<array<mixed>>|Iterator<array<mixed>> $rows, ExportOptions $options = null): Export
```

`Workbook::fromRows` makes a workbook with one sheet that has every row of `$rows`. Call `download`, `save`, `to` or `bytes` on the result to write it.
`$options` has the workbook options and the sheet options. `sheet` is the name of the sheet, and the default is `'Sheet1'`.

**Returns** `Export`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-workbook-sheet"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook->sheet`

```nvs skip
$workbook->sheet(string $name, SheetOptions $options = null): Sheet
```

`sheet` starts a new sheet named `$name` and returns it. The sheet before it is finished, and you cannot add rows to it after this.
When the rows have keys, the first row shows them in bold, with a filter, and stays at the top. `header`, `headerStyle`, `freeze` and `autofilter` change this.

**Returns** `Sheet`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-workbook-define"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook->define`

```nvs skip
$workbook->define(string $name, string $reference): Workbook
```

`define` gives the cells at `$reference`, such as `'Orders!$C$2:$C$9'`, the name `$name`. A formula can then use the name.

**Returns** `Workbook`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-workbook-finish"></a>
#### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook->finish`

```nvs skip
$workbook->finish(): Written
```

`finish` writes the end of the file and sends the last part. Call it once, after the last row.
A workbook that is never finished is not a valid file. A download that is never finished is cut off.

**Returns** `Written`

<a id="core-novis-spreadsheet-written"></a>
### `Novis\Spreadsheet\Written`

Keywords: constructor


| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$template` | `Filling` |  |
| `$source` | `mixed` |  |
